a31.speaker: Dr Maluke Letete, CBL Governor
a31.speech: Characterized the situation as a "huge economic challenge" facing the global economy; stated that the Committee heavily considered financial market developments to guide its policy decisions. ; "During discussions, the Committee noted that global economic performance was mixed in the first quarter of 2025. While major economies grew, momentum was uneven. The United States and the United Kingdom experienced slowing growth, weighed down by weaker consumer and government spending." ; "In contrast, the Euro area remained steady, buoyed by domestic demand, while the Japanese economy was lifted by strong exports. The Chinese economy benefited from targeted stimulus measures, and India's growth was driven by manufacturing and construction." ; Citing the International Monetary Fund, highlighted a downgrade in the global growth forecast for 2025: "Global growth is now projected at 2.8 percent in 2025, a downgrade from the earlier projection of around 3.3 percent. This revision results from rising trade tensions and deepening protectionism, which are dampening investment and confidence." ; Emphasized the challenging environment for Lesotho, citing risks such as volatile financial markets, unclear policy directions globally, slow productivity growth, and escalating geopolitical tensions. ; On inflation, noted divergent patterns across major economies: "In China, inflation was driven largely by weak domestic demand and trade tensions, while India experienced easing inflation due to lower food prices."

a31.speaker: Central Bank of Lesotho (Monetary Policy Committee)
a31.speech: Noted that growth in neighbouring South Africa is expected to remain subdued, hampered by weak domestic demand and global trade uncertainty, though labour markets remained broadly stable as of April. ; Observed a modest inflation increase in South Africa attributed to food and transport costs. ; Noted that most central banks have cut interest rates to stimulate growth but remain cautious due to persistent inflationary risks and global trade uncertainties linked to US tariffs. ; Noted that Lesotho's economy contracted by 5.3 percent in the first quarter of 2025, driven by weak consumption, reduced government spending, and underperformance in transport and construction, though manufacturing and financial services showed some resilience. ; Reported that net international reserves (NIR) increased by approximately $40.3 million to $1.069 billion as of May 21, driven by water royalties and SACU receipts. ; Decided to revise the NIR target floor from $840 million to $830 million, and cut the CBL rate from 7.25 percent to 7.0 percent per annum. ; Noted the withdrawal of $91 million in US foreign aid (equivalent to M1.7 billion), which previously supported health, education, and agriculture sectors.

a159.speaker: Experts (unnamed)
a159.speech: Warn that without robust systems for management and upkeep, the nation risks squandering value faster than it builds, and that the pressing question now is not how much Uganda constructs, but how effectively it preserves what already stands.

a205.speaker: Hamada Keiji, Ambassador of Japan to Mozambique
a205.speech: Announced on Thursday (27) in Maputo that his country's government will continue to work in the Mozambican government's priority areas, particularly in the sectors of education, health, human resource capacity-building for youth employment, investment, humanitarian aid and support for the stabilisation of security in Cabo Delgado province.

a205.speaker: Hamada Keiji, Ambassador of Japan to Mozambique
a205.speech: "The development of liquefied natural gas (LNG) in the province will contribute significantly to the country's economic independence and we will work together with Japanese companies, the government of Mozambique and partner countries."

a205.speaker: Hamada Keiji, Ambassador of Japan to Mozambique
a205.speech: "This year is a special year for Mozambique and Japan. For Mozambique it marks the 50th anniversary of its independence; for Japan it is the 50th anniversary of its official assistance to Mozambique."

a205.speaker: Hamada Keiji, Ambassador of Japan to Mozambique
a205.speech: Noted that the first TICAD was held at a time when the international community's interest in Africa was declining after the end of the Cold War and served as a catalyst to revive interest in Africa ; "It was also the pioneer of the many forums with Africa that exist today and we look forward to the participation of the President of the Republic, Mr Daniel Chapo."

a848.speaker: A former USAID official and a health official in Kenya
a848.speech: According to them, without U.S. funding, distribution from the warehouse, which stocks all U.S. government-donated HIV medicine to Kenya, has ceased, leaving supplies of some drugs worryingly low.

a848.speaker: Alice Okwirry, HIV patient in Nairobi
a848.speech: "I was just seeing death now coming," said the 50-year-old who was diagnosed with HIV in 2008 and has a 15-year-old daughter, Chichi, who is also HIV-positive ; "I told Chichi: what about if you hear the drugs are doomed?" Okwirry said, growing emotional. "She told me: Mom, I'll be leaning on you."

a848.speaker: US State Department
a848.speech: Issued a waiver last month exempting funding for HIV treatment from the freeze.

a848.speaker: Mackenzie Knowles-Coursin, former deputy head of communications for USAID, East Africa (resigned Feb. 3 in protest at the dismantling of the agency)
a848.speech: Said the USAID payments system in Kenya is down after the cuts, meaning contractors who implement the programmes cannot be paid ; "Projects are left wondering: 'Well, how am I going to resume activities if you're not paying me money?'" ; "The waivers that have been given are really waivers on paper." ; Added that in Kenya, officials in Washington have not authorised the release of money required to distribute the $34 million worth of medicine and equipment at the warehouse ; Told Reuters the commodities at the warehouse include 2.5 million bottles of ARVs, 750,000 HIV test kits and 500,000 malaria treatments.

a848.speaker: Kenyan government document seen by Reuters
a848.speech: According to it, about $10 million is needed for that distribution.

a848.speaker: Mission for Essential Drugs and Supplies (MEDS) website
a848.speech: Says the Christian charity that runs the warehouse supplies drugs to some 2,000 clinics nationwide.

a848.speaker: USAID
a848.speech: Referred a request for comment to the State Department, which did not respond.

a848.speaker: Mission for Essential Drugs and Supplies (MEDS)
a848.speech: Did not respond to requests for comment.

a848.speaker: Deborah Barasa, Kenya's Health Minister
a848.speech: Said she expected her government to mobilise funds to allow the supplies at MEDS to be released within two to four weeks. "We have identified the resources that are required," she said in an interview ; Said there would be enough Dolutegravir to last five months and Nevirapine to last eight months once the MEDS stocks were released.

a848.speaker: World Health Organization (data)
a848.speech: According to it, Kenya has the seventh-largest number of people living with HIV in the world, at around 1.4 million.

a848.speaker: A health official in Kenya (anonymous, asked not to be named because of the sensitivity of the matter)
a848.speech: Said stocks of two critical HIV treatments, Dolutegravir and Nevirapine, were low but did not know exactly how much remained nationwide.

a848.speaker: Nelson Otwoma, director of the National Empowerment Network of People Living with HIV/AIDS in Kenya
a848.speech: Said that for the time being, some patients can only get refills of their ARVs for one week at a time.

a848.speaker: Marco Rubio, US Secretary of State
a848.speech: On Monday said the Trump administration has cancelled more than 80% of all USAID programmes.

a848.speaker: Kenyan government's council on syndemic diseases (internal brief seen by Reuters)
a848.speech: Estimated last month that the U.S. cuts had created funding gaps of around $80 million.

a848.speaker: John Mbadi, Kenya's Finance Minister
a848.speech: Told senators last week that the government was reviewing whether to allocate emergency funding to compensate for U.S. aid cuts before it delivers the 2025/26 budget in the coming months.

a900.speaker: Philippe Kuessan-San Creppy, new UNHCR Representative in Djibouti
a900.speech: Praised the inclusive approach of the Djiboutian Social Development Agency (ADDS), underlining its central role in improving the living conditions of vulnerable populations: “ADDS is not only a key partner, it is also a hope for many vulnerable people, particularly women, children and youth. I explored with interest your community-based approach, which is a true model of holistic action.”

a900.speaker: Mahdi Mohamed Djama, Director General of the Djiboutian Social Development Agency (ADDS)
a900.speech: Insisted on the importance of treating refugees with the same dignity and the same rights as Djiboutian citizens; he also highlighted the essential role of UNHCR funding, stressing that it brings a glimmer of hope to displaced populations: “For us, refugees are full citizens. They have a right to education, to protection and to health. We work with them, as well as with host communities, to create development infrastructure and income-generating activities. Our goal is to empower these populations and give them back hope”, he said, expressing the wish that the coming year 2025 will be filled with hope regarding their joint collaboration.

a900.speaker: Mahdi Mohamed Djama (ADDS Director General) and Philippe Kuessan-San Creppy (UNHCR Representative)
a900.speech: Agreed during their discussions to strengthen their partnership, commitments that reflect a shared ambition to promote inclusive and sustainable development serving all the inhabitants of Djibouti.

a912.speaker: Millennium Challenge Corporation (MCC)
a912.speech: Has expressed its satisfaction with the operational systems reforms carried out by the sixth phase government in various areas including the strengthening of democracy, good governance and human rights.

a912.speaker: Dan Barnes, MCC Director of Policy and Evaluation
a912.speech: Said that in a period of three years of the sixth phase government, the corporation has been satisfied with various measures taken by Tanzania which have accelerated the economic development in the country ; said following the reforms, the US Congress has approved for Tanzania to continue benefiting from MCC funding.

a912.speaker: Mahamoud Thabit Kombo, Minister for Foreign Affairs and East African Cooperation
a912.speech: Said that Tanzania will continue to respect and cherish the strong relationship it has with the US for over six decades, while cooperating in various sectors including education, health, trade and investment, agriculture, energy, tourism, technology, defense and mining.

a912.speaker: Mahamoud Thabit Kombo, Minister for Foreign Affairs and East African Cooperation
a912.speech: Stressed that Tanzania will continue to uphold and implement the principles of democracy, good governance and human rights, which are shared values between Tanzania and the US.

a919.speaker: World Health Organisation (WHO)
a919.speech: Has called on the Nigerian government to strengthen the use of research and evidence in designing health financing policies that can accelerate progress towards achieving Universal Health Coverage (UHC).

a919.speaker: Robert Marten, Unit Head at Alliance for Health Policy and Systems Research, WHO
a919.speech: Said Nigeria faced peculiar challenges in health financing that required domestic solutions: “We are interested in reframing health financing as an investment and mobilising domestic resources to achieve UHC here in Nigeria” ; “This is not a unique goal as many countries are looking at it, but what is unique is Nigeria’s particular challenges” ; highlighted the urgent need to raise primary healthcare spending from $7 to $30 per person and to increase government health allocations from eight to 15 per cent of national expenditure ; stressed the importance of reducing out-of-pocket health spending by scaling up enrolment in the National Health Insurance Authority (NHIA) ; stressed that while there is consensus on what needed to be done, the how remained unclear, which is where health policy and systems research is crucial.

a919.speaker: Robert Marten, Unit Head at Alliance for Health Policy and Systems Research, WHO
a919.speech: Cited global examples, including India’s rollout of the world’s largest tax-funded health insurance scheme, which now covered 500 million people, and reforms in countries such as Rwanda, Mexico, Ghana and Taiwan that had embedded research into policy cycles ; said Nigeria could adapt lessons from those countries by prioritising local research capacity, fostering partnerships between policymakers and researchers, and institutionalising evidence-based decision-making ; said reforms succeed when they are backed by credible local institutions, measurable quick wins, multisectoral collaboration, and sustained trust between government, academia, and development partners ; “This is a moment in time for Nigeria to step up. Global health financing commitments are shrinking, but Nigeria has world-class expertise and leadership.”

a919.speaker: Iziaq Salako, Minister of State for Health and Social Welfare
a919.speech: Announced plans to enrol at least 44 million Nigerians into the National Health Insurance Scheme by 2030 as part of new measures to expand financial protection and reduce out-of-pocket spending on healthcare ; added that the ministry is considering legislation to double BHCPF funding from one to two per cent of consolidated revenue, alongside efforts to enrol 44 million Nigerians into the National Health Insurance scheme by 2030.

a919.speaker: Iziaq Salako, Minister of State for Health and Social Welfare
a919.speech: Said President Bola Tinubu has directed policies to strengthen domestic financing and protect vulnerable Nigerians; noted that the President has continued to emphasise that a strong health system is vital for national growth and has therefore directed the implementation of several interconnected policies to achieve universal health coverage: “The government has consistently funded the Basic Health Care Provision Fund (BHCPF) and introduced emergency allocations to cushion the suspension of foreign aid.”

a964.speaker: Ibrahim Nur, managing director of the Southern Denkalia sub-zone
a964.speech: stated that 111 people, including 37 women, were elected as area administrators, managing directors, and village coordinators ; highlighted that awareness-raising activities conducted prior to the elections played a significant role in ensuring a successful electoral process; he also commended the strong participation of residents and urged the newly elected officials to serve the people with dedication.

a964.speaker: Newly elected officials (Southern Denkalia sub-zone)
a964.speech: expressed their commitment to fulfilling their responsibilities with diligence, honoring the trust placed in them by the community.

a964.speaker: Idris Mohammed, administrator of the Hagaz sub-zone
a964.speech: reported that the elections were conducted in 14 administrative areas; as a result, 14 area administrators, including one woman, 14 managing directors, including 13 women, and 67 village coordinators, including 24 women, were elected ; also called on the newly elected officials to diligently serve the people who entrusted them with these responsibilities.

a1006.speaker: Bloomberg News, citing people familiar with the matter
a1006.speech: Reported on Wednesday that a United States initiative aimed at increasing the electricity supply in Africa had been dismantled by the administration of President Donald Trump after more than a decade of work; the report adds, citing anonymous sources, that almost all Power Africa programmes are on the list of programmes to be discontinued and the majority of its staff have been laid off, and that some remaining programmes, notably those aimed at connecting projects with American companies, could be retained under the responsibility of other US agencies.

a1006.speaker: US State Department spokesperson (cited by Bloomberg)
a1006.speech: "Every programme is under review with the goal of restructuring aid to serve American interests."

a1006.speaker: US State Department official (anonymous, to Bloomberg)
a1006.speech: "Programmes that serve our nation's interests will continue. By contrast, those that are not aligned with our national interests will not," a department official told Bloomberg in response to questions.

a1006.speaker: US State Department
a1006.speech: An email sent to the US State Department's office seeking comment did not receive an immediate response.

a1058.speaker: Kwame Nkrumah, first President of Ghana
a1058.speech: Famous for the quote, "Seek ye first the political Kingdom and all else shall be added unto you." ; Was also a strong advocate for African Unity, arguing that such a unity "would have an overall economic planning on a continental basis which would increase the industrial and economic power of Africa."

a1058.speaker: The Lagos Plan of Action (1980 document)
a1058.speech: The Plan urged Africa to move away from overreliance on raw materials as the biggest export and instead focus on industrialization amongst other initiatives; in addition, it called for greater continental integration.

a1058.speaker: Study of regional integration efforts within Africa
a1058.speech: A study of regional integration efforts within Africa reveals that despite public statements, there are still many barriers that countries place on the path of increased trade with their neighbours.

a1136.speaker: Malawi Government
a1136.speech: Has described as a "huge relief" the decision by United States Secretary of State Marco Rubio to issue a waiver for life-saving humanitarian assistance during a 90-day pause in foreign aid while Washington undertakes a review.

a1136.speaker: Donald Trump, US President
a1136.speech: Announced the pause to allow US authorities to review foreign aid contributions to gauge their alignment with Trump's 'America First' foreign policy.

a1136.speaker: Marco Rubio, US Secretary of State (memo released on Tuesday)
a1136.speech: Defined life-saving humanitarian assistance as core life-saving medicine, medical services, food, shelter and subsistence assistance, supplies and reasonable administrative costs as necessary to deliver such assistance. "This waiver does not apply to activities that involve abortions, family planning conferences, administrative costs… gender or DEI (diversity, equity and inclusion) ideology programmes, transgender surgeries or other non-life saving assistance."

a1136.speaker: Moses Kunkuyu, Malawi Government spokesperson
a1136.speech: Expressed gratitude to the American government. Said Malawi was making strides to stand on its own but that it was not there yet and that any assistance to help the people of Malawi was an investment. He said the waiver gave Malawi a breather as it worked on strategies to take care of the health of its own people. "Natural disasters and pandemics have pushed us back in as far as public health is concerned. We are not there, [in terms of] standing on our own, yet. We still need development partners to help our health budget."

a1136.speaker: Khumbize Kandodo Chiponda, Malawi Health Minister
a1136.speech: Expressed gratitude to the American government. Said Malawians should not despair as there were enough stocks of essential drugs such as ARVs, antimalarials and tuberculosis drugs. She said "we are happy" with the waiver.

a1136.speaker: Malawi Health Equity Network
a1136.speech: Also welcomed the US government's decision to grant a waiver on its 90-day freeze of foreign aid, allowing life-saving humanitarian assistance to continue.

a1136.speaker: George Jobe, executive director of the Malawi Health Equity Network
a1136.speech: Said the decision was timely. "This is a huge relief as the US government has listened to the pleas we have made over the past days that the 90-day freeze must spare critical areas in health." According to Jobe, any loss of life due to the freeze would have been irreversible, even if exemptions were granted later. Jobe urged Washington to ensure continued support for vital interventions, including the supply of drugs and vaccines, even after the 90-day period expires. "The US government has contributed significantly to Malawi's health and livelihoods sectors, and we believe they would not want to compromise the huge gains already attained."

a1136.speaker: United States Agency for International Development (USAID) (stop-work order and award suspension notice)
a1136.speech: Issued a stop-work order (SWO) and award suspension notice to its implementing partners in Malawi. The directive requires implementing partners to cease activities under existing agreements and halt any expenditures related to ongoing projects. Affected organisations were instructed to notify their sub awardees of the suspension and take measures to minimise costs already incurred.

a1290.speaker: Dr. Layli Maparyan, President of the University of Liberia
a1290.speech: summarized her accomplishments during her February visit to the United States at a press conference on Wednesday, March 5, 2025. Among her key achievements, she highlights the signing of two important Memoranda of Understanding (MoUs) with U.S.-based institutions: the first with MBC to offer an online Hospitality Management Certificate program, and the second with CSU centering on a healthcare administration program.

a1290.speaker: Dr. Layli Maparyan, President of the University of Liberia
a1290.speech: outlines UL's "Plans to increase the number of faculty members holding PhDs". She also reveals efforts to secure slots for UL faculty from UCL (University Consortium for Liberia) member institutions, a move intended to enhance faculty development and academic excellence.

a1290.speaker: Dr. Layli Maparyan, President of the University of Liberia
a1290.speech: mentions discussions with Kennesaw State University (KSU) on potential collaboration on developing a conflict resolution master's or PhD program at UL, with a trauma track, and regarding the Georgia Tech Online Master's Program in Computer Science, noting that this partnership could lead to future announcements about collaborative educational opportunities.

a1290.speaker: Dr. Layli Maparyan, President of the University of Liberia
a1290.speech: says she received a letter of support from the President of the University of Georgia (UGA), reaffirming their commitment to collaborate with the UL in advancing higher education here.

a1310.speaker: Hirsi Jama, Somalia's State Minister for Education
a1310.speech: "Education is the cornerstone of Somalia's progress, fostering critical thinking and empowering women for economic development. Thanks to USAID and the UK, these young women are equipped with vital skills, setting the foundation for a brighter future where informed, educated women contribute significantly to health, nutrition, and societal well-being."

a1310.speaker: Taylor Tinney, Acting Deputy Chief of Mission at the U.S. Embassy in Mogadishu
a1310.speech: Expressed pride in the collaborative efforts with the Government of Somalia and the UK: "This ceremony is a testament to the potential within each graduate, and we remain committed to fostering opportunities that empower girls and elevate communities."

a1310.speaker: Nick Jaques, UK Deputy Ambassador
a1310.speech: Emphasized the importance of unlocking talents and skills: "The girls graduating today are an important reminder of the millions of girls across the country seeking a decent education. Unlocking their talents and skills is crucial to building a safer and stronger Somalia tomorrow."

a1310.speaker: Nuura Mustaf, State Minister of Education, Culture, and Higher Education
a1310.speech: Congratulated the graduates and expressed gratitude to all involved in the transformative initiative: "Education is the key to empowering our youth and building a brighter future for Somalia."

a1310.speaker: Ummy Dubow, CARE Somalia Country Director
a1310.speech: Highlighted the impact of the AGES program in empowering vulnerable girls: "This graduation marks the achievements of these girls, underscoring the impact of USAID and FCDO's support in realizing their life aspirations."

a1396.speaker: Events and trade show industry professional (anonymous online message to the Kigali Convention Center)
a1396.speech: "Dear KCC (Kigali Convention Center) leaders, I work in the events and trade show industry and I am interested in touring your Kigali Convention Center. I will be in Rwanda July 25 through August 12. I will be working with a female leadership and education effort. I would also like to connect with the leadership of the KCC. Please let me know a couple options to tour this center."

a1396.speaker: Roland Dieterle, German architect who designed the Kigali Convention Complex (on meeting President Kagame)
a1396.speech: "I noticed to be talking to a very bright and intelligent person, and somebody not just talking but also listening, and I was really surprised that he was not just telling me what is in his vision but he was really curious to learn from me how I perceive the country and the opportunities for the country." ; "Of course he told me about where the country is, what has been the past, and what the challenges for the future are, and the challenges of the present time. He explained to me in detail about his vision for the country's Vision 2020 to end this transition from an agricultural country to a service country of the 21st century." ; "During my first visit to Rwanda, His Excellency the president asked me to visit the National Museum in Butare, so I got the opportunity to learn about the traditional roots and fascinating culture of the country – a chance which most visitors don't have. This gave us the idea to integrate an innovative exhibition facility into this complex in Kigali – the Rwanda Experience Center was born."

a1396.speaker: Roland Dieterle, German architect (on his first impressions of Rwanda)
a1396.speech: Admits that he knew little-to-nothing about the country before he came: "It was the first time, and honestly speaking I was totally, totally surprised in a very positive way because it's such a wonderful nice country and you see the landscape, you see so many things which you didn't automatically associate with Africa. It's totally different than what people normally know of Africa, and particularly about Rwanda. It's a totally different country in comparison to what normally the media tell us about."

a1396.speaker: Roland Dieterle, German architect (on the design concept and the dome)
a1396.speech: "The colors is also something we found in the country, like people are wearing clothes, also buildings are wearing an envelope like cloth, and our idea was to translate the tradition of how to wear clothes, particularly female dressing into the building. And we believe after the sad story of the country, we believe that bringing fresh colors, bright colors and also something which is delightful to people is something that is positive for the new identity of Rwanda." ; "First of all we developed the scheme which we believe is not just an import of ideas from outside like we see in many buildings and urban developments in Africa, but we had a phase of very intense investigation of the art and crafts here, how is the architecture, the climate – all these things had to be investigated by us and we derived the concept out of those findings," adding that the dome structure is the most important and significant element of the project. ; "Honestly speaking it is also the most complex part of this project, and people immediately understood why we did this – there is a tradition of round buildings in the country, particularly the rebuilt King's Palace which is also a dome-shaped building. Of course it's not just blowing up the same architecture, it's our own language which we developed, but people immediately understand that this is something which has to do with their own tradition." ; "When I came to Kigali and was asked to make a design for the convention center I went around Kigali and I saw that there's no real center in the town, and also there's not a real land mark building. So immediately the idea came up to make a design which is also a landmark building for the city." ; "It was very interesting for me to find the theme for this design here in Rwanda."

a1396.speaker: Critics from Germany and Europe
a1396.speech: Had accused Dieterle of importing an overly luxurious (and expensive) engineering concept to a country that is only rising from the ashes of political and economic ruin.

a1396.speaker: Roland Dieterle, German architect (responding to critics)
a1396.speech: Believes that the Kigali Convention Complex is a perfect model for sustainable urban development in Africa: "In practice it is not realistic for a country to develop itself from the grassroots level to the high-tech level", adding: "It needs landmark projects that demonstrate Rwanda's success in order to reach an international level, as well as to show highly educated Rwandans that they can be optimistic about finding perspectives in their own country."

a1443.speaker: World Food Programme (WFP)
a1443.speech: has warned for years that it is facing shortfalls in the contributions from governments it relies on for funding, and on Monday it announced that it is closing its office in South Africa due to U.S. President Donald Trump's cuts in foreign aid.

a1443.speaker: John Garang, refugee from South Sudan in Kakuma camp
a1443.speech: held up a roughly 4 litre pot: "This is the container they are now using to measure beans and oil and the other one for rice. And this is equivalent for one month for your food. Assume you don't have another income, it's only this. Is this enough for you," he asked.

a1554.speaker: Dr Remy Pale, Permanent Secretary of the Coordination of Agricultural Sectoral Policies (SP/CPSA), Ministry of Agriculture, Animal and Fisheries Resources of Burkina Faso
a1554.speech: On Burkina Faso's objectives at the Dakar forum: "The African Food Systems Forum is a crossroads for all the countries of Africa. It is a crossroads for sharing experiences, for learning, but also for networking. It was therefore appropriate for Burkina to be there, not only to make known what it does best, but also to learn from the various countries taking part in this forum, to see what we can capitalise on in the search for our food sovereignty and in the endogenous development process we have embarked upon." He added that the delegation had an obligation to carry Burkina's voice, to accompany the young Burkinabe who came to showcase their innovations, and to forge partnerships with countries and institutions.

a1554.speaker: Dr Remy Pale, Permanent Secretary of the Coordination of Agricultural Sectoral Policies (SP/CPSA), Ministry of Agriculture, Animal and Fisheries Resources of Burkina Faso
a1554.speech: On the Burkinabe experiences presented: "We first emphasised the fact that we are a Sahelian country dependent on rainfall. And in order to build a food system that is robust and resilient, we need first to work on the basic factors of production." He cited the presidential initiative for agriculture and food self-sufficiency and the Agro-pastoral and Fisheries Offensive, water control, hydro-agricultural developments, the supply of improved seed varieties and quality fertiliser, and the reforms creating ONBAH, the extension of SONATER's mandate, SOBIMAP, the transformation of SONAGESS into a purchasing centre, the Dumu Ka Fa Fund, Faso-Guulgo, Faso-Kosam and Faso abattoir: "All these reforms mean that today Burkina has all the basic instruments needed to embark serenely on the process of its food sovereignty."

a1554.speaker: Dr Remy Pale, Permanent Secretary of the Coordination of Agricultural Sectoral Policies (SP/CPSA), Ministry of Agriculture, Animal and Fisheries Resources of Burkina Faso
a1554.speech: On agroecology: Said the session on agroecology coincided with other ministerial meetings and he could not take part as the minister's representative, but other ministry staff, NGOs and development associations attended those sessions to share Burkina's experience. "For my part, we took advantage of the exchanges with the various stakeholders to return to Burkina Faso's experience in agroecology." He noted that the state company SOBIMAP also puts bio-inputs on the market, and that agroecological practices are promoted by his department in full understanding with NGOs, cooperatives, umbrella bodies and development associations.

a1554.speaker: Dr Remy Pale, Permanent Secretary of the Coordination of Agricultural Sectoral Policies (SP/CPSA), Ministry of Agriculture, Animal and Fisheries Resources of Burkina Faso
a1554.speech: On the sessions attended: Said Burkina took part in the ministerial session on livestock, the round table of ministers of Agriculture, Livestock and Water with partners - at the end of which "the partners reaffirmed their alignment with national priorities" - and a session on trade and regional markets, where "we reaffirmed our country's current orientation of reducing or even eliminating the share of raw products in our trade with the outside world. The minimum is to carry out primary processing in order to add value and create jobs. Moreover, this processing must be oriented as a priority towards satisfying domestic consumption."

a1554.speaker: Dr Remy Pale, Permanent Secretary of the Coordination of Agricultural Sectoral Policies (SP/CPSA), Ministry of Agriculture, Animal and Fisheries Resources of Burkina Faso
a1554.speech: On bilateral meetings held in the margins: Said he held exchanges with the Malian Minister of Agriculture and the technical adviser representing the Nigerien Minister of Agriculture, and met the regional coordination of the United Nations system "to clear up the misunderstanding about Burkina Faso's flagships, notably the one on food and agri-food systems. This meeting made it possible to affirm and reposition the State's national leadership in carrying strategic projects, including investments in agriculture." He also met Africa Rice, which with AGRA has established a partnership to support seed production in several countries including Burkina; the Coordinator of the Coalition for African Rice Development (CARD) based in Ethiopia; and the FAO regional coordinator based in Dakar.

a1554.speaker: Dr Remy Pale, Permanent Secretary of the Coordination of Agricultural Sectoral Policies (SP/CPSA), Ministry of Agriculture, Animal and Fisheries Resources of Burkina Faso
a1554.speech: On the young Burkinabe agricultural entrepreneurs: "These young people are full of innovations and use technology in agriculture better than their predecessors. They can change the structure of our agriculture and make this sector a source of jobs and wealth for young people who still hesitate to return to the land... Today, they have worthily represented Burkina Faso at this Forum. They presented quality products and managed to establish contacts. They need support." He added that with the representative of the Minister of Youth they agreed to meet again to create a framework for exchanges between the two ministries.

a1554.speaker: Dr Remy Pale, Permanent Secretary of the Coordination of Agricultural Sectoral Policies (SP/CPSA), Ministry of Agriculture, Animal and Fisheries Resources of Burkina Faso
a1554.speech: On the overall assessment: "We are very satisfied with our participation." He cited carrying Burkina's voice at the forum, forging partnerships with institutions and research bodies, reaffirming the need to respect the State's national leadership over development initiatives, the business contacts obtained by young entrepreneurs - including a young woman agri-food processor who won over large Senegalese distribution chains and Faycal Palenfo of "Faso Poulet", who won second prize in the innovation competition with a solar incubator - and learning from other countries, notably in East Africa: "In conclusion, the assessment is very satisfactory for Burkina."

a1556.speaker: Judge Ramon Maasdorp, Windhoek High Court
a1556.speech: Granted Xinfeng's urgent application on 27 June to prevent Alweendo from cancelling the licence and forcing it to vacate the mine by 31 May; however, he did find prima facie evidence indicating that Xinfeng may have committed plagiarism and fraud in its initial application for the licence. He found that the minister did not have the power to cancel the licence in accordance with Namibia's Minerals (Prospecting and Mining) Act, and that Alweendo should have approached the courts to get the award of the application reviewed.

a1556.speaker: Xinfeng Investments (through its lawyers, Nambili Mhata Legal Practitioners)
a1556.speech: Said it secured consent from the Daure Daman Traditional Authority (DDTA) to explore in the authority's jurisdiction in 2022, and that an environmental clearance certificate was issued to Longfire Investments following a thorough environmental assessment impact study. “The JV represents a strategic partnership between two Namibian companies, Xinfeng being the investor with international experience. The JV is aimed at transferring knowledge and skills, offering employment opportunities and contributing to the sustainable development of Namibia.” ; "The JV's objective is to build a mineral beneficiation plant that will be managed by Namibians, with assistance from Xinfeng Investments' experts. The current mining operations for the mining claims are set to benefit all parties involved. There is a lease agreement with the DDTA for the surface rights, in which the JV commits to support the community with proceeds from the mining claims."

a1663.speaker: Amy Diaz, United States Chargé d'Affaires in Malawi
a1663.speech: In a strongly worded statement, condemned the violence, describing the events as sickening. She criticised the apparent failure of state security forces to protect citizens exercising their constitutional rights. "What was particularly appalling was the failure of the Malawi Police Service and the Malawi Defence Force to carry out their duties to protect their fellow citizens. The fundamental duty of any government is to ensure that citizens can freely exercise their rights under the constitution."

a1663.speaker: British High Commission and other international missions (joint statement)
a1663.speech: Echoed the U.S. condemnation, urging Malawian authorities to act decisively. The joint communiqué called on the government to uphold the rule of law, protect all citizens, and launch a thorough investigation into the violent incidents.

a1663.speaker: Malawi's security agencies and government officials
a1663.speech: Have yet to issue a statement more than 24 hours after the attack occurred.

a1727.speaker: Three diplomats (anonymous)
a1727.speech: Told AFP on Wednesday that the International Atomic Energy Agency's 35-nation board of governors has passed a resolution criticising Iran's lack of cooperation with the UN nuclear watchdog ; told AFP that the resolution was carried by 20 votes in favour -- including the United States, which initially was reluctant for fear of aggravating Middle East tensions -- with 12 abstentions and one country not participating.

a1727.speaker: IAEA Board of Governors resolution (confidential document obtained by AFP)
a1727.speech: Reiterates it is "essential and urgent" that Tehran provide "technically credible explanations" for the presence of uranium particles found at two undeclared locations in Iran ; states that "A continued failure" by Iran to provide full cooperation on the years-long probe "may necessitate" a comprehensive assessment by IAEA chief Rafael Grossi ; says Iran has to "reverse its withdrawal of the designations of several experienced Agency inspectors", and "without delay" reconnect the cameras used to monitor nuclear activities ; notes the "concerns" surrounding "recent public statements made in Iran... regarding its technical capabilities to produce nuclear weapons and possible changes to Iran's nuclear doctrine".

a1727.speaker: Tehran (Iranian government)
a1727.speech: Has already threatened "a serious and effective response", and slammed the censure motion as "devoid of any legal, technical and political basis".

a1727.speaker: European powers at the IAEA Board of Governors debates
a1727.speech: Denounced Iran's expansion of its nuclear programme "to alarming levels" as "unprecedented for a state without a nuclear weapons programme".

a1727.speaker: Britain, France and Germany (the E3), separate statement
a1727.speech: "Iran's escalating nuclear activities significantly harm international security and undermine the global non-proliferation architecture."

a1727.speaker: International Atomic Energy Agency (IAEA)
a1727.speech: According to the IAEA, Iran is the only non-nuclear weapon state to enrich uranium to the high level of 60 percent -- just short of weapons-grade -- while it keeps accumulating large uranium stockpiles.

a1727.speaker: Tehran, Moscow and Beijing (joint statement quoted by Iran's official news agency IRNA)
a1727.speech: Called on "Western countries to show political will... and take the necessary steps to resume the implementation" of the 2015 nuclear deal.

a1727.speaker: United States (national statement to the IAEA board)
a1727.speech: Rejected that assertion as "a tired and transparent gambit" ; "Iran refused a deal when it was possible, continued with activities that negated the chance for that deal, and now makes baseless statements to obfuscate the history."

a1747.speaker: Nicolas Haysom, Special Representative of the UN Secretary-General for South Sudan (briefing to the Security Council)
a1747.speech: Stressed while briefing ambassadors at the Security Council on Wednesday that while the country's citizens have been patient, they expect progress: "There is a strong desire for the leaders to focus on the benchmarks set out in the peace agreement - without further delay." ; urged South Sudan's leaders to accelerate security sector reform, electoral preparations, and reform of the constitution and judicial processes: "The clock is already ticking on the extended transitional period. Decision-makers need to tackle several issues simultaneously and immediately."

a1747.speaker: Nicolas Haysom, Special Representative of the UN Secretary-General for South Sudan
a1747.speech: Said that despite some achievements major gaps persist, especially concerning elections scheduled for December 2026: while a framework for security sector management and a national community violence reduction strategy have been adopted, critical conditions remain unmet including the full deployment of unified security forces, voter education, and a code of conduct between political parties and other stakeholders: "We have not yet seen the previously promised harmonized workplan with an operational timetable for elections," adding that delays in government funding and decision-making are further impeding progress.

a1747.speaker: Nicolas Haysom, Special Representative of the UN Secretary-General for South Sudan
a1747.speech: Noted that communal violence remains a major driver of insecurity, disproportionately affecting vulnerable populations including women and children, and that recent clashes between armed groups in Western Equatoria, along with widespread reports of illegal checkpoints, highlight the fragility of the security environment.

a1747.speaker: Nicolas Haysom, Special Representative of the UN Secretary-General for South Sudan and head of UNMISS
a1747.speech: Briefed on logistical challenges faced after the Government requested the mission vacate part of its headquarters within 45 days, describing the demand as imposing "significant costs" and logistical hurdles that UNMISS is not currently equipped to manage, and noting that restrictions on peacekeeper movement in some areas continue to limit the mission's ability to provide security and humanitarian support.

a1747.speaker: Nicolas Haysom, Special Representative of the UN Secretary-General for South Sudan
a1747.speech: Concluding his briefing, reaffirmed the UN's commitment to standing "shoulder-to-shoulder" with the people of South Sudan on their path to stabilisation and democratisation.

a1747.speaker: South Sudanese authorities
a1747.speech: Announced in September last year, under the latest extension of the transition, that general elections are scheduled to take place in December 2026.

a1747.speaker: United Nations / 2025 Humanitarian Needs and Response Plan
a1747.speech: The 2025 Humanitarian Needs and Response Plan aims to reach 5.4 million people with life-saving assistance and protection, but funding remains a critical challenge; the UN is appealing for $1.7 billion to meet urgent needs this year.

a2190.speaker: Scientists
a2190.speech: Say the blood of a US man who deliberately injected himself with snake venom for nearly two decades has led to an "unparalleled" antivenom.

a2190.speaker: Tim Friede, US man who injected himself with snake venom
a2190.speech: Said that he had "completely screwed up" early on when two cobra bites in quick succession left him in a coma ; "I didn't want to die. I didn't want to lose a finger. I didn't want to miss work."

a2190.speaker: Tim Friede, US man who injected himself with snake venom
a2190.speech: Explained that his motivation was to develop better therapies for the rest of the world: "It just became a lifestyle and I just kept pushing and pushing and pushing as hard as I could push - for the people who are 8,000 miles away from me who die from snakebite."

a2190.speaker: Tim Friede, US man who injected himself with snake venom
a2190.speech: Said reaching this stage "makes me feel good" ; "I'm doing something good for humanity and that was very important to me. I'm proud of it. It's pretty cool."

a2190.speaker: Dr Jacob Glanville, chief executive of biotech company Centivax
a2190.speech: "Immediately I was like 'if anybody in the world has developed these broadly neutralising antibodies, it's going to be him' and so I reached out" ; "The first call, I was like 'this might be awkward, but I'd love to get my hands on some of your blood'."

a2190.speaker: Dr Jacob Glanville, chief executive of biotech company Centivax
a2190.speech: Said the breadth of protection was "unparalleled" and that it "likely covers a whole bunch of elapids for which there is no current antivenom."

a2190.speaker: World Health Organization
a2190.speech: Identified 19 elapids as being among the deadliest snakes on the planet.

a2190.speaker: Research study published in the journal Cell
a2190.speech: Identified two broadly neutralising antibodies that could target two classes of neurotoxin; in experiments on mice, the antivenom cocktail meant the animals survived fatal doses from 13 of the 19 species of venomous snake, with partial protection against the remaining six.

a2190.speaker: Prof Peter Kwong, researcher at Columbia University
a2190.speech: "I think in the next 10 or 15 years we'll have something effective against each one of those toxin classes."

a2190.speaker: Prof Peter Kwong, researcher at Columbia University
a2190.speech: "Tim's antibodies are really quite extraordinary - he taught his immune system to get this very, very broad recognition."

a2190.speaker: Prof Nick Casewell, head of the centre for snakebite research and interventions at the Liverpool School of Tropical Medicine
a2190.speech: Said the breadth of protection reported was "certainly novel" and provided "a strong piece of evidence" that this was a feasible approach ; "There is no doubt that this work moves the field forwards in an exciting direction" ; but cautioned there was "much work to do" and that the antivenom still needed extensive testing before it could be used in people.

a2222.speaker: Brigadier-general Luís Barroso, EUMAM MOZ Mission Force Commander
a2222.speech: Briefed the delegation of the European Parliament on EUMAM MOZ' roles, capabilities, mission, current activities and the main ongoing projects within the Headquarters.

a2342.speaker: Worldwide movements supporting the Palestinian cause (participants in the "Maghreb Convoy of Resilience", including doctors and lawyers)
a2342.speech: Decided to express active solidarity with their "oppressed brothers" ; all are demanding dignity for their brothers in Gaza in particular and in Palestine in general.

a2342.speaker: Organisers of the "Maghreb Convoy of Resilience"
International Criminal Court (ICC)
a2342.speech: Issued arrest warrants against Israel's leaders, namely Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu and his former defence minister, Yoav Gallant.

a2564.speaker: Malawi Congress Party (MCP)
a2564.speech: Reacted defiantly, staging what it termed a “victory march” in Lilongwe city.

a2564.speaker: Malawi Electoral Commission (MEC)
a2564.speech: Has strongly condemned the MCP’s demonstration, describing it as an “unholy act” that undermines the integrity of the electoral process.

a2564.speaker: MEC officials
a2564.speech: Have urged all political parties to remain patient and await the official announcement of results through formal channels.

a2585.speaker: Health Ministry of the Gaza Strip (daily report)
a2585.speech: reported today that more than 100 Palestinians were killed and another 200 wounded in Israeli attacks in the Gaza Strip in the last 24 hours; according to hospital records, 103 bodies arrived at morgues during Wednesday and 219 wounded were treated at local health centres. According to the ministry, and based on updated data considered reliable by the UN, at least 56,259 people have died and more than 132,000 have been wounded since the start of the Israeli offensive, following the Hamas attacks of 7 October 2023. According to a count by the ministry, more than 500 Palestinians have been killed by Israeli gunfire near humanitarian aid distribution points since the GHF began operating at the end of May.

a2585.speaker: Medical sources cited by the Spanish news agency EFE
a2585.speech: said that among the dead counted in the last 24 hours are at least 45 who were victims of a series of attacks on Gaza City, including seven members of the same family, and that another 12 people were killed by Israeli gunfire while seeking aid at food distribution points managed by the Gaza Humanitarian Foundation (GHF) in the south and centre of the Gaza Strip.

a2585.speaker: Benjamin Netanyahu, Prime Minister of Israel
a2585.speech: said on Wednesday night that he had given the Israeli army 48 hours to draw up a new plan for managing humanitarian aid in northern Gaza, which, according to him, Hamas is appropriating.

a2675.speaker: Emerico Adjovi, member of the Beninese Human Rights Commission (CBDH)
a2675.speech: Rejoices: "From now on, Benin will be able to sit at the same table as the so-called great democracies."

a2675.speaker: Isidore Clement Capo-Chichi, President of the Beninese Human Rights Commission (CBDH)
a2675.speech: "Our ambition, in the future, is to manage to open the other branches in the remaining departments. In the long term, we plan to cover all 77 communes."

a2675.speaker: Isidore Clement Capo-Chichi, President of the Beninese Human Rights Commission (CBDH)
a2675.speech: Makes an important clarification: the accreditation is not definitive; it is evaluated every five years and the country can lose it when one of the accreditation criteria is lacking.

a2675.speaker: Isidore Clement Capo-Chichi, President of the Beninese Human Rights Commission (CBDH)
a2675.speech: Expressed his gratitude to the American Bar Association, to USAID and to the United States Embassy, which support the institution in its actions, and praised the government for having "placed trust in men whom it did not choose but appointed".

a2675.speaker: Representatives of civil society organisations (CSOs), youth organisations, USAID and the Embassy of the United States of America
a2675.speech: Unanimously welcomed the results obtained by the CBDH ; in particular, the technical and financial partners reassured the CBDH of the continuation of their support.

a2778.speaker: United States government
a2778.speech: Says it wants to make sure its aid is being used effectively, while it reviews its foreign assistance programmes.

a2791.speaker: Ghana Statistical Service, Annual Household Income and Expenditure Survey Quarter Three Labour Bulletin
a2791.speech: Indicated that the average rate of unemployment in the country had risen to 14.7 per cent in the first three quarters of 2023. It said the number of unemployed youth aged between 15 and 35 rose from about 1.2 million to over 1.3 million during the same period, specifying that the rate among females was consistently higher than males.

a2791.speaker: graphic.com.gh poll
a2791.speech: 60 per cent of respondents to a poll run by graphic.com.gh said the economy ranked as their priority as far as the December 7 polls were concerned.

a2791.speaker: Statista (economy and politics platform)
a2791.speech: According to Statista, South Africa is expected to record about 30 per cent unemployment rate in 2024, while Djibouti and Eswatini have unemployment rates of 28 and 25 per cent respectively.

a2791.speaker: Statista (economy and politics platform)
a2791.speech: Published in July 2024 that almost half of Ghana's population works in the service sector, and around 33 per cent work in agriculture. The population is relatively young, with only around three per cent of the total population aged 65 or older.

a2791.speaker: National Democratic Congress (NDC) manifesto
a2791.speech: "The 24-Hour Economy policy aims to transform Ghana into an import-substitution and export-led economy," the manifesto says, while promising a Women's Development Bank, a National Apprenticeship Programme, an ‘Adwumawura' Programme aimed at facilitating the creation, tracking and mentoring of a minimum of 10,000 businesses annually, digital jobs initiative involving a $3 billion investment, a million coders programme, among others.

a2791.speaker: New Patriotic Party (NPP) manifesto
a2791.speech: States that the number one priority is to stimulate businesses and create jobs, with a strong focus on the private sector. "Our commitment to you is to invest in the growth of Ghanaian businesses, create millions of secure jobs for the youth, ensure individual and collective prosperity, safe communities, and to offer you a problem-solving leadership of integrity," the document states. Those commitments, it said, would be delivered by sustaining and expanding "Ghana's rebounding economy", creating new jobs, including training a million, among other interventions.

a2791.speaker: Alan Kyerematen, Independent presidential candidate and leader of the Movement for Change
a2791.speech: Said in his Great Transformation Plan he would focus on job creation, particularly for the youth, adding that his 10-Point Youth Empowerment Plan he introduced recently was aimed at addressing the high unemployment rates in the country. The plan included supporting youth-owned businesses, installing 100,000 health booths to be managed by the youth, assisting the youth in mining communities to own small-scale mining companies, and promoting youth involvement in agriculture and industrialisation.

a2791.speaker: Nana Kwame Bediako (Cheddar), Leader of the New Force Movement and Independent Presidential candidate
a2791.speech: In his “12 Pillars for Economic Freedom” said he would generate 8 million jobs over the 10 years when he is elected as President, focusing on several key sectors, including industries, mineral resources and agriculture.

a2791.speaker: Professor John Gatsi, Professor of Finance, Chartered Economist and Barrister at the University of Cape Coast
a2791.speech: Said governments could deal with unemployment through the expansion of existing businesses, through new opportunities and new venture creations. "So, if you are having an economy that is expanding in an inclusive manner, then you have a policy that is truly going to address unemployment, especially for the young people. So, the first policy that we should see, that should give us hope that we are going to tackle the unemployment situation is the productivity of the country. (We have to analyse) Whether we have policies that are focusing on productivity of the economy because that is what is going to bring about business expansion. That is what is going to create new venture opportunities and businesses. Then we can add institutional reforms to job creation," Prof. Gatsi told the Daily Graphic.

a2791.speaker: Professor John Gatsi, Professor of Finance, Chartered Economist and Barrister at the University of Cape Coast
a2791.speech: Said both the NDC and the NPP had talked about digital economy, specifically in relation to training up to a million young people in coding. "So, that is one area that if we are able to do, can give some respite," he said. The lecturer, however, stressed that "all the youth who are unemployed cannot be IT experts, cannot be focusing on IT to get jobs. So, we also need to expand job opportunities through economic engagement in other sectors".

a2791.speaker: Professor John Gatsi, Professor of Finance, Chartered Economist and Barrister at the University of Cape Coast
a2791.speech: Said manifesto content that put some focus on agriculture was good as an alternative to the other proposed interventions. "Looking at the risk in agriculture, bringing on board coordinated approach from regulated institutions like the Bank of Ghana, Ministry of Finance, Ministry of Food and Agriculture to focus on coordinating in terms of agriculture so that the sector could serve as an instrument for currency protection and also serve as an instrument for expansion of agribusinesses and the rest. So, there are some indicators in both poster parties' manifestos that show that there is some understanding as to how to approach the canker of unemployment to see that we defeat it," Prof. Gatsi said. "The question is can these proposals contained in the respective manifestos address the subject of unemployment? The proposals can only address some aspects of unemployment. And we need much more than just the IT skills to solve unemployment. So, the new ideas in agriculture, for example, can also bring about job creation," he added.

a2791.speaker: Eugene B.G. Bawelle, lecturer and sustainable banking consultant
a2791.speech: Said the central themes of the manifestos of the two major political parties dwelt on the creation of jobs. "Both NDC and NPP, for example, have promised to train a million young people in coding. The NDC goes a step further to talk about its human resource gap analysis within Ghana's public sector, as well as the establishment of various financial interventions to support small and medium scale businesses," he analysed. Mr Bawelle explained, however, that the major problem was "the effective implementation of these interventions when these parties come to power". He said examples of how badly such interventions had been implemented in the past were replete, "hence, even though the issue of unemployment seems to have a considerable amount of attention in the manifestos, the main concern will be how the political parties will efficiently implement these policies to curb the growing unemployment menace".

a2791.speaker: Isaac Doku, Economics Department of the University of Education, Winneba
a2791.speech: Diagnosed the unemployment situation as partly caused by weak laws and institutions in the country. He said the NPP, for instance, had proposed to deal with youth unemployment by creating a youth employment fund dedicated to projects and programmes that engage young people in productive work; facilitate mentorship and training programmes that connect youth with experienced professionals in various sectors; and digital job creation. "Interestingly, most youthful entrepreneurs in Ghana today are looking for opportunities to exit the country. Their capital has been usurped by the constant depreciation of the cedi and constant rise in their production cost. What surprises me the most is that new foreign companies entering the Ghanaian market are allowed to operate tax free for several years. Meanwhile, Ghanaians operating in their own country will begin to pay taxes with several harassment from revenue authorities immediately they begin operation." ; "The major opposition party is hitting largely on a 24-hour economy policy of three shifts to encourage and support businesses; Adwumawura programme; digital jobs and one million coders programme. As explained by the 2024 Nobel Prize winners why there is large income inequality between rich and poor countries, they mentioned that societies with poor rule of law and institutions that exploit the population do not see growth. Until we strengthen our institutions to work and pay realistic wages to employees, there is no hope. Corruption, armed robbery and galamsey are commonplace in Ghana because minimum wage is GHc18.15 compared to the price of bread of GHc20." He added that the youth are "still impoverished even if he is employed", and so find it better to engage in other illegal activities or emigrate. "That is why most youths are interested in employment that comes with power and authority, like the police and military, to use them to their advantage," he added.

a2791.speaker: Professor Godfred Bokpin, Professor of Finance and Economics at the University of Ghana, Legon
a2791.speech: Said it was good that the political parties had recognised the growing unemployment in the country. "They've all also articulated how they are going to address that. In fact, if you count the number of times that the word jobs appear in the manifestos, it's quite a lot. And then also, you see that, especially the two main political parties, there's a shifting attention on the youth. There are specific interventions that they have all mentioned. That will create jobs. The question that all of them have not been able to answer is how is this going to be financed? And what are the timelines? First year, second year, third year, what are the timelines? What are the specific interventions and operational strategies?" ; He said if the parties would be able to translate all their promises into reality, the jobs potential would be a lot. "But I can assure you, the four years will be too short to implement even 40 per cent of the promises they've all made," he emphasised.

a2791.speaker: Professor Godfred Bokpin, Professor of Finance and Economics at the University of Ghana, Legon
a2791.speech: Said while the NDC's 24-hour economy policy would need time to materialise, the NPP's intention to rely on the private sector looked questionable. "Private sector is not for charity," he said. "Entrepreneurs don't go into business to create jobs. It's never their goal. Entrepreneurs go into business to create value. So their preoccupation is not to solve unemployment." ; The lecturer said while tax reforms being proposed by the major parties, including the scrapping of e-levy and betting tax, were good, it would lead to revenue shortfalls, which would need to be addressed through some other interventions. "And then also, we are under an IMF-supported programme. What it means is that within the first year of implementation or the first two years, you may not be able to have that scope to manoeuvre your way through in implementing many of those promises. So the four years is too short to even implement 40 per cent of the promises they have made," he said.

a2951.speaker: Bianca Odumegwu-Ojukwu, Nigerian Minister of State for Foreign Affairs
a2951.speech: Urged the United States of America to follow laid down convention on deportation of persons in repatriating immigrants in their country; bemoaned the emotional and financial pains that many Nigerians in the United States were already experiencing since the new administration indicated its resolve to repatriate some categories of people from the US; asked the US Government to find a way of ameliorating the trauma of those to be deported including allowing them ample opportunity to retrieve their assets in America: “With the new administration in the US, we want a situation where there will be commitments. If there will be repatriation, we want dignified return.” ; “At the moment, we’re told that about 201 Nigerian nationals are in US immigration camps, and about 85 have been cleared for deportation.” ; “Will there be any way of ameliorating their pains? This has been of great concerns to not just Nigerian nationals in the US but family members in Nigeria who depend on them for survival, children whose school fees are paid for by these diasporans.” ; “We are asking as a country whether they will be given ample time to handle their assets or will they just be bundled into planes and repatriated? It will really be traumatic especially for those who had not committed any violent crime.”

a2951.speaker: Bianca Odumegwu-Ojukwu, Nigerian Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (statement issued by her Special Assistant on Communication & New Media, Magnus Eze)
a2951.speech: Stated that the effect was far-reaching even to the hinterlands of Nigeria where for instance, several families including children relied on remittances from the US for their survival and education.

a2951.speaker: Bianca Odumegwu-Ojukwu, Nigerian Minister of State for Foreign Affairs
a2951.speech: Urged Washington DC to reconsider its possible suspension of the Drop Box Visa Policy such that Nigerians who had been travelling to the US for genuine reasons would not have to suffer unduly in procuring US Visa; urged the US Government to issue a statement clarifying its actual position on the Drop Box system to assuage the concerns of anxious Nigerians.

a2951.speaker: Bianca Odumegwu-Ojukwu, Nigerian Minister of State for Foreign Affairs
a2951.speech: Disclosed that about 14,000 Nigerian students are in the US, with parents in Nigeria, and said these parents were worried whether there will be any change in student policy by the new US administration.

a2951.speaker: Bianca Odumegwu-Ojukwu, Nigerian Minister of State for Foreign Affairs
a2951.speech: Expressed worry that the future of USAID was not known, saying: “We can’t say whether it’s outright suspension. A lot of NGOs are worried to get clarifications. We will just make that appeal on behalf of the NGOs in Nigeria, even less than a month into the 90 days review, there have been concerns. And I know before the completion of the review, there’s already humanitarian issues in Nigeria and Africa. We will make an appeal that this initiative be preserved, even if it’s abrogated as an agency, there must be a way of keeping the ideals to ensure that the poor beneficiaries in the communities, not just in Nigeria but Africa, are not abandoned.”

a2951.speaker: Bianca Odumegwu-Ojukwu, Nigerian Minister of State for Foreign Affairs
a2951.speech: Called for injection of more impetus in the bilateral relations between Abuja and Washington DC; noting that Nigeria and US had not done well in the area of trade especially post-COVID-19, she called for investments in the mining sector, saying diversification of investments would engender boost in export to the US; called for the reactivation of the ‘Silent Secretariat’ where the two countries assessed their bilateral relations.

a2951.speaker: Bianca Odumegwu-Ojukwu, Nigerian Minister of State for Foreign Affairs
a2951.speech: Explained that the foreign policy of the President Bola Ahmed Tinubu-led Administration which focuses on Democracy, Development, Demography and Diaspora (4-Ds) was on course, pointing out that the federal government was committed to citizen diplomacy: “One other area is not just diaspora but diplomacy, people-to-people contacts. So, the issue of illegal migration is there but the current administration is determined about citizen diplomacy. We want to know how our people in diaspora are doing. We have some of the in prisons abroad, the administration is concerned about their welfare.” ; said that Nigeria needed strategic partnerships to tackle the demographic issue of unemployment which triggers illegal migration known as Japa syndrome in Nigerian parlance ; said that it was in line with the 4-Ds foreign policy of Nigeria, that despite the Sahel crisis, the free movement policy of ECOWAS was still in place: “ECOWAS has been at its best, so, one has to appreciate that even with the exit of these states, yet free movement within the region is still there. The immigration has not closed the borders.”

a2951.speaker: Richard Mills Jr., US Ambassador to Nigeria
a2951.speech: Said that he looked forward that the bilateral relations between both countries will get quite broader ; “I think this administration will concentrate more on trade and commerce. This relationship is strong and we want it sustained.” ; also spoke on AGOA which ends September this year but noted that it is left for the parliamentary group to push for its renewal ; congratulated Amb. Odumegwu-Ojukwu on her recent appointment as minister.

a2951.speaker: Richard Mills Jr., US Ambassador to Nigeria
a2951.speech: Said that the Drop Box Visa Policy has not been suspended, explaining that whenever there is a change in administration, policies are renewed; assured that the position of the new US Government on the USAID, Drop Box Visa system and others, would be known in due course.

a2951.speaker: Richard Mills Jr., US Ambassador to Nigeria
a2951.speech: Acknowledged that the USAID did some specifics particularly in life-saving in the health sector, humanitarian issues like mother-child issue: “Some of these NGOs are feeling the pains, but the situation is being reviewed.”

a2951.speaker: Richard Mills Jr., US Ambassador to Nigeria
a2951.speech: Expressed concerns over democracy in Africa, noting the exit of three Sahel States from ECOWAS as well as the challenge of counter-terrorism.

a2951.speaker: Richard Mills Jr., US Ambassador to Nigeria
a2951.speech: On the deportation of Nigerian immigrants, he said: “Those to be repatriated would be dropped in Lagos. There wouldn’t be room for whether it should be in Port Harcourt or Abuja.” ; “The first group will be convicted prisoners. Those who committed crimes and are in US prisons. Some of them are those who have clearly violated US immigration laws. They appealed but were denied yet they are still in the US. They have committed immigration crime, people who have been ordered to leave.”

a3033.speaker: United States Embassy in N'Djamena
a3033.speech: Issued a firm warning to its nationals on Friday 6 June, calling on all American citizens to immediately reconsider any plans to travel to Chad, even if they already hold a valid visa; recalled that entry into Chadian territory is at the sole discretion of the local authorities, specifying that it will not be able to intervene to facilitate the entry of nationals in a private capacity; and recommended that its nationals regularly monitor the official websites of the Chadian government, consult the embassy's updates, follow the local media and adopt a posture of caution and discretion during their stay.

a3033.speaker: American authorities
a3033.speech: Justify the decision to ban entry from twelve countries, including Chad, as of 9 June by a strengthening of internal security measures, after an attack that recently occurred in the state of Colorado.

a3033.speaker: Mahamat Idriss Déby Itno, President of Chad (Facebook post)
a3033.speech: Confirmed the reciprocal measure in a message published on his Facebook page, denouncing an American decision that was “unjust and discriminatory,” stating: “Chad has neither planes to offer, nor billions of dollars to give, but Chad has its dignity and its pride.”

a3033.speaker: Several human rights organisations
a3033.speech: Have denounced the American policy, which they accuse of mainly targeting African or Muslim-majority countries.

a3092.speaker: City of Cape Town
a3092.speech: According to the City of Cape Town, 81 homes in Town Two were gutted, leaving 192 people homeless.

a3092.speaker: Khaziwe Dyantyi, Khayelitsha resident who lost her home
a3092.speech: Told GroundUp that she had grabbed her three-year-old daughter after hearing neighbours shouting that shacks were on fire ; "I rushed out of my shack with my kid and left all my belongings inside except my pyjamas and my gown… I have no materials to rebuild my burnt shack" ; said she had lost all her belongings, which included a bedroom set, fridge, clothing, washing machine, and laptop ; "I rely on my child's grant for survival most of the time as my bosses only ask me to work sometimes."

a3092.speaker: Vuyiswa Makhaphela, Khayelitsha resident who lost her home
a3092.speech: Said they had struggled to breathe as their shack was already engulfed in smoke by the time they woke up ; "I used my grandchildren's grant to buy them stationery two days ago. We have no clothes to wear now. My kids have to go to school, but they have no uniforms and stationery. The youth rebuilding my shack with the damaged materials are hungry, but I have no food to give them as my groceries are also burnt."

a3092.speaker: Vuyiswa Makhaphela, Khayelitsha resident who lost her home
a3092.speech: Said that the high density in the area contributed to why so many people were affected by the fire ; "The firefighters came quickly, but could not enter our area because we don't have roads and our shacks are too close to each other. This is why people could not pull out big things like fridges, sofas and beds."

a3092.speaker: Lubabalo Msuthu, South African National Civic Organisation (Sanco) chairperson in Town Two
a3092.speech: Said dozens of the fire victims were still being housed by a local church; he said it was sad that most people had already bought uniforms and groceries with their social grants last week ; "Now they have all burnt. We only saw food coming from the government. The fire victims need more support."

a3092.speaker: Thando Pimpi, Ward councillor
a3092.speech: Said he would write letters to school principals asking them to be lenient with affected children who will not have uniforms and stationery; he said there were plans by the City of Cape Town to de-densify the area ; "We are planning to remove a certain number of people, place them somewhere and build roads. This will happen after the Silver Town Project beneficiaries have moved into their places."

a3092.speaker: City of Cape Town Disaster Risk Management officials (statement)
a3092.speech: Said in a statement that Gift of the Givers and Sassa was providing humanitarian assistance ; "The Electricity and Water & Sanitation [departments] will attend to damaged infrastructure, while Solid Waste will remove fire debris. Home Affairs was also activated to assist residents with identity documents."

a3116.speaker: Nelnam Koumtingue, International Monetary Fund (IMF) resident representative
a3116.speech: Says Malawi has made progress in some areas in line with the four-year $175 million (about K306 billion) Extended Credit Facility (ECF), but challenges still remain. ; “While progress has been made in some areas, challenges remain. The IMF last conducted a programme review mission in May 2024 and discussions between the IMF and the Malawian authorities have continued. However, the review has not yet been completed and under our policies, ECF arrangements automatically terminate before their scheduled end if no programme review has been completed over an 18-month period.”

a3116.speaker: Nelnam Koumtingue, International Monetary Fund (IMF) resident representative
a3116.speech: In a written response on Friday, he said the ECF programme approved on November 14 2023, was meant to support improved macroeconomic stability, promote export growth, enhance foreign exchange availability and build foreign exchange reserves.

a3116.speaker: A handbook of IMF facilities for low-income countries (document)
a3116.speech: Indicates that ECF arrangements will automatically terminate before their scheduled terms if no programme review has been completed over an 18-month period.

a3116.speaker: International Monetary Fund (IMF)
a3116.speech: According to the IMF, one of the most urgent goals of the current ECF arrangement is to support the authorities’ commitment to restoring macroeconomic stability and creating an environment of low or moderate inflation and a stable exchange rate.

a3116.speaker: Capital Hill (Malawi Government)
a3116.speech: Said the series of reforms Malawi has implemented were tough, but necessary to convince development partners that the Malawi Government is committed to reforms to revitalise the ailing economy, including raising the policy rate and devaluing the kwacha.

a3116.speaker: Lazarus Chakwera, President of Malawi
a3116.speech: In December last year, in response to a question from Mulanje South West lawmaker George Chaponda, who is also Leader of Opposition in Parliament, dismissed suggestions that the ECF is derailed, stating that it is “broadly on track”.

a3116.speaker: Betchani Tchereni, Secretary to the Treasury
a3116.speech: Revealed that the Malawi Government had initiated discussions with the IMF to review some targets under the ECF programme, including disparities between programme assumptions and conditions on the ground, necessitating a reassessment of previously agreed targets.

a3116.speaker: Betchani Tchereni, Secretary to the Treasury
a3116.speech: He was yet to respond to our questions on the current status of the ECF programme. (non-response)

a3116.speaker: Velli Nyirongo, Centre for Green Economy in Developing Countries global lead
a3116.speech: In an interview on Sunday said the delays in debt restructuring and rising expenditure constrain efforts to rebuild foreign exchange reserves, putting the ECF programme in jeopardy. ; “Given the current geopolitical challenges and the decline in donor aid, Malawi needs the ECF.”

a3116.speaker: Lingalireni Mihowa, Oxfam in Malawi country director
a3116.speech: Is on record as having said while the government has managed expenditure, revenue targets fall short, a development that points to some budget assumptions not materialising.

a3505.speaker: Shareholders of Rural-Metro Corporation
a3505.speech: Said their bankers, lured by lucrative financing fees, had pressed the board of Rural-Metro Corporation to bless the deal without adequate valuation analysis.

a3505.speaker: US judge / 2014 court ruling in the Rural-Metro case
a3505.speech: A judge agreed and in 2014 ordered the adviser to pay 75.8 million dollars, about 83pc of the investors' losses, for having “aided and abetted” directors who breached their fiduciary duties.

a3505.speaker: America's Office of the Comptroller of the Currency
a3505.speech: Lists the tricks that blossom when mandates overlap. They steer underwriting business to affiliates, favour in-house products over superior outsider options and trade on privileged information.

a3505.speaker: Post-mortems across jurisdictions after the 2008 crash
a3505.speech: Found that “overboarding” dulled independent challenge and bred groupthink.

a3505.speaker: Academic studies
