a3505.speech: Link dense interlock networks to lower shareholder returns and higher volatility.

a3505.speaker: Ethiopian Capital Market law (2021) and the ESX rulebook
a3505.speech: Repeat global platitudes, instructing directors to avoid conflicts “in fact and appearance” and to remain independent of the entities they oversee.

a3505.speaker: International Organisation of Securities Commissions
a3505.speech: Warns that even a whiff of bias can repel foreign capital from emerging markets.

a3508.speaker: Kelly Ann Shaw, trade lawyer at Hogan Lovells and former White House trade adviser during Trump's first term
a3508.speech: “This is the single biggest trade action of our lifetime.” ; Told a Brookings Institution event on Thursday that she expected the tariffs to evolve over time as countries seek to negotiate lower rates: “But this is huge. This is a pretty seismic and significant shift in the way that we trade with every country on earth.”

a3508.speaker: U.S. Customs and Border Protection (bulletin to shippers)
a3508.speech: Indicates no grace period for cargoes on the water at midnight on Saturday ; did provide a 51-day grace period for cargoes loaded onto vessels or planes and in transit to the U.S. before 12:01 a.m. ET Saturday, which need to arrive by 12:01 a.m. ET on May 27 to avoid the 10% duty.

a3508.speaker: Trump administration (published exemption list)
a3508.speech: Released a list of more than 1,000 product categories exempted from the tariffs, valued at $645 billion in 2024 imports, including crude oil, petroleum products and other energy imports, pharmaceuticals, uranium, titanium, lumber and semiconductors and copper.

a3648.speaker: Purported list obtained by The NEW DAWN (“University of Liberia Faculty and Staff listing as of June 2025”)
a3648.speech: Indicates that the cost saving measure is allegedly being proposed by the Interim Vice President for Finance and Fiscal Affairs, Dr. Lester Tenny, pending approval of UL President, Dr. Ophelia Maparyan; the list contains names of lecturers and professors, their dates of employment, dates of birth, gender, and current ages.

a3648.speaker: Critics (of the University of Liberia administration)
a3648.speech: Have accused Dr. Maparyan of importing nearly fifty (50) individuals, previously made redundant by USAID, and hurriedly placing them within the University of Liberia faculty structure, granting them academic ranks ranging from Assistant Professor to Associate Professor; suggest that to create space for these new appointees, she has directed Dr. Lester Tenny to force the retirement of selected professors, including several who have not yet reached the statutory retirement age; argue that these individuals represent decades of institutional knowledge, professional competence, and a commitment to the University's growth, contending that their forced retirement would be a direct blow to academic freedom, institutional memory, and the quality of education at the UL ; “The intent behind this scheme is to weaken independent voices within the faculty ranks, accommodate loyalists, who owe their positions to Dr. Maparyan's patronage. Also, this is intended to erode the integrity and autonomy of the University of Liberia as a public academic institution. Lastly, if this agenda succeeds, the University risks becoming an institution run by favoritism rather than merit, undermining its credibility nationally and internationally.”

a3648.speaker: Potential victim of the pending exercise, a University of Liberia faculty member (anonymous)
a3648.speech: Said the recent developments at the University of Liberia reveal a troubling scheme by the current administration under Dr. Ophelia Maparyan, and that a list of active, qualified, and experienced faculty members is being quietly prepared for premature retirement ; “The move appears less about academic reform and more about creating space for new appointees whose loyalty will be directed to Dr. Maparyan personally, rather than to the University as an institution. Such actions represent a dangerous precedent of political patronage and personal consolidation of power within an academic environment.”

a3648.speaker: Cllr. Noris Tweah, Vice President for University Relations, University of Liberia
a3648.speech: Said he was on a tennis court and had ended his working hours, therefore he couldn't speak to the matter: “Lincoln, it's after working hours and I am on the tennis court right now. I am saying to you, I am on the tennis court right now, and it's after working hours. The University is only paying me for working hours. I had a long day today. I am on the tennis court playing game, so I can't talk now” ; when contacted again on Tuesday, September 2, 2025 via direct calls and text messages, he declined to comment.

a3787.speaker: Badr Abdelatty, Egyptian Minister of Foreign Affairs
a3787.speech: Emphasised “the urgency of beginning the rapid recovery” and reconstruction of Gaza “with the presence of Palestinians” in the enclave, “in light of their attachment to their land and their absolute rejection of displacement” ; conveyed to US Secretary of State Marco Rubio “the full support of the Arab and Islamic worlds, as well as of the international community” for the presence of Palestinians in Gaza.

a3787.speaker: Egyptian Ministry of Foreign Affairs (statement)
a3787.speech: According to a statement, the two diplomats met in Washington.

a3787.speaker: Marco Rubio, US Secretary of State (via the US State Department)
a3787.speech: Thanked Abdelatty for “Egypt’s mediation efforts to secure the release of the hostages, maintain humanitarian aid deliveries in Gaza and accept medical evacuations,” US diplomacy reported.

a3787.speaker: Donald Trump, US President
a3787.speech: When receiving Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu in Washington last week, declared that the United States would “take ownership” of the Gaza Strip and “get rid of the destroyed buildings,” with the aim of developing the territory economically ; repeated that the inhabitants of Gaza could go and live in Jordan or Egypt, despite the opposition of those countries and many others, as well as that of the Palestinians themselves.

a3787.speaker: Donald Trump, US President
a3787.speech: In an excerpt from an interview released on Monday, said Palestinians would not have the right of return; asked by a Fox News reporter whether Palestinians would have the “right of return” to the war-devastated enclave once rebuilt, Trump replied: “No, they wouldn’t, because they are going to have much better housing” ; “In other words, I’m talking about building a permanent place for them, because if they went back now, it would take years to rebuild Gaza — it is not habitable” ; said the United States would build “beautiful communities” for the roughly two million inhabitants of the Gaza Strip: “It could be five, six or two. But we are going to build safe communities, a little bit away from where they are, where all the danger is” ; “We have to think of this as a real estate development for the future. It will be a beautiful piece of land. There will be no great expense.”

a3787.speaker: Israel (declaration of war)
a3787.speech: Declared war in the Gaza Strip on 7 October 2023 to “eradicate” the radical Hamas movement, hours after Hamas carried out an attack of unprecedented proportions on Israeli territory, killing about 1,200 people, mostly civilians.

a3956.speaker: Kaja Kallas, EU High Representative for Foreign Affairs (the bloc's top diplomat)
a3956.speech: Said the European Union and South Africa are forging closer ties after previous disagreements led to a frosty relationship ; "It is a time of building partnerships and strengthening the partnerships we have. Finding old friends and making new friends" ; "Whatever differences there were, I feel that they are in the past and we can settle them."

a3956.speaker: Kaja Kallas, EU High Representative for Foreign Affairs
a3956.speech: Earlier this week expressed support for South Africa's aims on climate and equality issues as this year's G-20 president.

a3956.speaker: Kaja Kallas, EU High Representative for Foreign Affairs
a3956.speech: Said that given the erratic nature of Trump's pronouncements, which have ranged from demanding Denmark sell Greenland to the US to offering South Africa's white Afrikaans minority refugee status in the US, countries are seeking closer relationships with the EU ; said multilateralism is under threat right now but this is an opportunity to develop further international law to be more inclusive of all the countries in the world ; "A lot of partners are turning to us because we are the reliable, the predictable partner. So that has value in these current turbulent times."

a3956.speaker: Kaja Kallas, EU High Representative for Foreign Affairs
a3956.speech: Said that, given the EU's own pressing demands, the bloc won't be able to step in to fill the gap left by the US cutting back on aid globally ; "Considering the steps that America has taken, then all the countries in the world who are in need and also organisations, multilateral organisations are at our door. We can't fill that void that the US is leaving because we don't have those funds."

a3956.speaker: Kaja Kallas, EU High Representative for Foreign Affairs
a3956.speech: Said the EU, given Trump's threats to withdraw military support at a time when Russia has caused the biggest conflict in Europe since World War II, needs to focus on defense spending because it faces an "existential threat."

a3956.speaker: Donald Trump, US President
a3956.speech: Falsely accused the nation of seizing private land, and has vowed to end US support for South Africa's fight against HIV, to which the US contributes more than $400 million a year.

a3956.speaker: Marco Rubio, US Secretary of State
a3956.speech: Snubbed the gathering citing issues including land and equality policies among his reasons for not going.

a3956.speaker: European Union Chamber of Commerce and Industry of Southern Africa
a3956.speech: According to the chamber, more than 1 000 European companies operate in the country, directly employing more than 350,000 people.

a4027.speaker: Thabo Mbeki, retired President of South Africa
a4027.speech: Said that in the past Africa had various institutions of young people, women and other groups that brought them together to discuss and build a good future for the continent, and that even the African Union (AU) and today’s higher education institutions have not resolved to seek an answer to the various obstacles to Africa’s growth; the disappearance of those institutions makes Africans lack unity in seeking a solution to the challenges of employment and development, and in the end foreign nations do it on their behalf: “Our continent must be self-reliant and must be interpreted by ourselves and not by the Chinese, the Indians, the Russians and the Americans.” ; “Unfortunately we Africans do not know this, and that is a big problem. President Kikwete and other people of his age ought to know — we had institutions that held us together, but now they no longer exist.”

a4027.speaker: Thabo Mbeki, retired President of South Africa
a4027.speech: Said there is no institution that brings young people together to have a joint force and give one statement as the youth of Africa: “How can we find an answer to questions about employment and the empowerment of young people? What I am saying is that young people too ought to be part of the people answering that question.” ; called for higher education institutions to restore the role of answering questions about how African countries can manage and use the freedom they have.

a4027.speaker: Thabo Mbeki, retired President of South Africa
a4027.speech: Asked participants to reflect on the importance and understanding of the continent’s main policies, especially those concerning youth development, and questioned how many people know them ; stressed that some of the commissions of the African Union have not worked effectively in countries such as Tanzania, something that shows the gap between institutional systems and actual results for citizens ; called on Africa’s political leaders to restore the spirit of accountability driven by a commitment to sacrifice for the community, as was the case during the liberation struggles.

a4027.speaker: Jakaya Kikwete, fourth-phase President of Tanzania
a4027.speech: Praised the vision of the Thabo Mbeki Foundation of an Africa that does not stand aside in the development of the world: “The fire of Africa’s renaissance has been stirred up again, and I call on leaders and stakeholders to carry out genuine reforms rather than superficial changes.”

a4027.speaker: Simon Shayo, Vice President for Sustainability (Africa) at AngloGold Ashanti
a4027.speech: Questioned why Africa belittles itself when comparing itself with other regions that are developing rapidly ; stressed the need to invest in knowledge and in the continent’s leadership in order to achieve a future decided by Africans themselves.

a4255.speaker: Ministry of Foreign Affairs, African Cooperation and Moroccans Residing Abroad of Morocco (communique)
a4255.speech: "The Kingdom calls on all Palestinian and Israeli parties to give Peace a chance and to demonstrate a sincere and constructive commitment, far removed from any circumstantial or opportunistic considerations." ; The communique adds that the Kingdom expresses the wish that this ceasefire agreement be fully respected, and that it allow an end to the attacks against civilians, the return of the displaced, and the smooth access of humanitarian aid in sufficient quantities ; The communique continues that the ceasefire agreement should open the way to a genuine peace process, allowing the establishment of a Palestinian State within the 1967 borders with East Jerusalem as its capital, living side by side and in peace with Israel.

a4255.speaker: King Mohammed VI of Morocco, President of the Al-Quds Committee
a4255.speech: Stressed, notably in His Royal Message to the last Arab Summit, that it is fundamental to avoid leaving one crisis only to enter another.

a4436.speaker: African Development Bank (AfDB), African Economic Outlook Report
a4436.speech: Has said it expects the local economy to grow by 3 percent in 2025, and further predicted that the Malawi economy could grow by 3.8 percent next year ; Says the growth will be driven by a recovery in agriculture and tourism, alongside gains from mining investments ; "On the demand side, growth will be bolstered by a rebound in exports and improved real incomes, supporting consumer spending and investment," the bank says ; According to AfDB, inflation is expected to decline to 23.8 percent by 2026, reflecting better food supply conditions ; "The fiscal deficit is projected to widen to 9.3 percent of GDP in 2025 before narrowing to 8.6 percent in 2026, as strict expenditure controls offset the underperformance of public revenues. Although stronger economic activity and higher consumer demand are likely to increase imports, the current account deficit is projected to shrink to 17.9 percent of GDP in 2025 and 16.9 percent in 2026, supported by higher export earnings," AfDB says.

a4436.speaker: African Development Bank (AfDB), African Economic Outlook Report
a4436.speech: Notes that key risks to the outlook include United States reciprocal trade tariffs and aid cuts, delays in resolving the debt crisis and climate-related shocks, which it says could undermine fiscal stability, infrastructure investments and agricultural recovery.

a4436.speaker: Akinwumi Adesina, outgoing AfDB president
a4436.speech: Notes that with properly sequenced reforms, Africa can mobilise an additional $1.43 trillion in domestic resources from its diverse forms of capital—fiscal, natural, financial, business and human—to accelerate inclusive and sustainable growth.

a4436.speaker: Reserve Bank of Malawi Monetary Policy Committee (MPC)
a4436.speech: At its recent Monetary Policy Committee meeting, the Reserve Bank of Malawi trimmed GDP growth for Malawi for 2025 from 4 percent in October last year to 3.2 percent; according to the MPC, the revision reflects weak agricultural performance due to delayed rainfall and prolonged dry spells in some parts of the country.

a4484.speaker: Agora Centre for Research (statement)
a4484.speech: Confirmed that their director, Agather Atuhaire, has been found alive at the Uganda-Tanzania border: "We are relieved to inform the public that she has been found. She was abandoned at the border by Tanzanian authorities. Further details will be shared later today. We extend our heartfelt gratitude to everyone who stood in solidarity during this time. Your efforts truly made a difference."

a4484.speaker: Amb. Col (Rtd) Fred Mwesigye, Uganda's High Commissioner to Tanzania
a4484.speech: "I would like to confirm that @AAgather has reached home and has been received by the family."

a4484.speaker: Boniface Mwangi, Kenyan human rights activist (post on X)
a4484.speech: Revealed that he and Atuhaire were tortured by Tanzanian security: "The last time l was in the same space with @AAgather was Tuesday morning. We had been tortured, and we were told to strip naked and to go bathe. We couldn't walk and were told to crawl and go wash off the blood. We were handcuffed and blindfolded, so l didn't even see her, but l heard her groaning in pain as they barked orders at us. Any attempt to speak to each other during the night we were tortured was met with kicks and insults. We were removed from the torture location in different vehicles." ; "Our torturers were acting on orders from a 'state security' employee who came to immigration offices and followed us to Central Police Station and ordered we should be taken to a secret location to be given a 'Tanzanian treatment.' That man assaulted me in the presence of three lawyers from Tanganyika Law Society, and identifying him might help us find where Agather is being kept." ; "He scared the three lawyers, and they left us at Central Police Station, where we were removed while handcuffed and blindfolded. He is a man of average height, had short hair with waves and light brown skin, and was overweight; he has a sagging potbelly. On that day he was wearing a black suit, black shoes, a white shirt and no tie. One of the lawyers said he is state security and reports directly to @SuluhuSamia If anyone is holding Agather, it's that man and Suluhu. Let's bring Agather home to her family."

a4641.speaker: Andualem Admassie (PhD), Director-General of the Higher Education & Relevance Quality Agency
a4641.speech: Stated that discussions began last week and that the independence of the Agency should not be impaired; noted that the Agency reports to the Ministry, which is also where all the public universities it is expected to regulate report. "This is a conflict of interest. While the Agency had the mandate to shut down institutions, there have been issues with interference. Institutions are being given protection where the Agency wants to act, in both private and public spheres."

a4641.speaker: Andualem Admassie (PhD), Director-General of the Higher Education & Relevance Quality Agency
a4641.speech: Said the Agency wants to play a more proactive role in protecting the community, as shutting down institutions takes place after time and money have been wasted, and that with the number of private institutions, campuses and programmes a better system needs to be in place. "There are millions of students enrolled, and the institutions are working with billions of Birr, which isn't properly systemised." ; "The number reported by private institutions was half a million initially, but we pressured them to divulge correct figures" - and said the current number is still debatable.

a4641.speaker: Andualem Admassie (PhD), Director-General of the Higher Education & Relevance Quality Agency
a4641.speech: Said the Agency cannot be the accountant and the auditor simultaneously, adding that the proposal for its restructuring is being undertaken internally based on different recommended studies from international organisations like USAID.

a4641.speaker: Tirussew Teferra (Prof.), lecturer at Addis Abeba University's College of Education & Behavioural Studies
a4641.speech: Said that as private education institutions are mostly business-oriented, it is important that the Agency is taking steps to become more autonomous in its regulatory role. "There are instances where private institutions are opening up without staff. They just use the profile of other institutions."

a4641.speaker: Tirussew Teferra (Prof.), lecturer at Addis Abeba University's College of Education & Behavioural Studies
a4641.speech: Said there needs to be more than regulation for the growth of quality. "Higher education institutions need to be more competitive. There should also be more focus given to making higher education institutions centres of excellence." ; Cited the example of the University of Haramaya as potentially being a centre of excellence for agriculture, and recommended that the work toward quality start at an early stage in the learning-teaching process, as this can produce students that can teach themselves.

a4690.speaker: Malawi Council of Churches (MCC)
a4690.speech: Has urged President Lazarus Chakwera to humbly accept defeat in the September 16, 2025, General Election.

a4690.speaker: Reverend Billy Gamah, MCC Chairperson
a4690.speech: Said that based on partial results released by the Malawi Electoral Commission last night, “the table can not change to deliver victory” for Chakwera ; added that an early concession would be a statesmanlike move, sending a strong message to supporters to accept the outcome peacefully ; “We believe that conceding early, even before the official announcement, will show maturity, promote peace, and help the nation move forward without violence or unnecessary tension.”

a4690.speaker: Bakili Muluzi, former President of Malawi
a4690.speech: Made similar appeals to Chakwera to concede, which the church’s call follows.

a4751.speaker: Mosaique FM, Tunisian radio station
a4751.speech: Reported that on 21 February, 11 Tunisian students received a notification ordering them to leave United States territory after their studies at American universities were suspended ; specified that the 11 Tunisian students had been given a seven-day deadline to leave United States territory ; emphasises Donald Trump's decision to freeze foreign aid for 90 days.

a4751.speaker: IREX (International Research and Exchanges Board) website
a4751.speech: The TJSP is presented as a programme that “aims to foster economic growth, stability and democratic development in Tunisia by equipping a network of young Tunisians with essential skills that can lead to positive professional and community change.”

a4751.speaker: Elon Musk, head of the Department of Government Efficiency
a4751.speech: Described USAID as a “nest of Marxist vipers.”

a4751.speaker: Several Egyptian media outlets
a4751.speech: Reported at the beginning of February the suspension, for a period of 90 days, of the funding of their educational scholarships financed by USAID.

a4918.speaker: United Nations report on children and armed conflict in Burkina Faso
a4918.speech: Records “2,483 grave violations against 2,255 children” between 1 July 2022 and 30 June 2024, some having suffered several abuses; “Deadly armed attacks against civilians have intensified and have seriously worsened the humanitarian situation,” with more than two million people internally displaced; estimates that “6.3 million people, including 3.4 million children, need humanitarian assistance,” particularly nutrition, health, protection and education ; states that “1,386 children, some as young as eight months old, were killed and maimed, notably by explosive devices”; confirms “the abduction of 592 children, mainly girls,” as well as “the recruitment and use of 257 children,” mostly boys ; notes that “Twenty girls were raped, one of whom died as a result of a gang rape” ; reports that the transition government validated a handover protocol with the UN to “ensure that children allegedly associated with armed forces and groups are transferred to civilian child protection services,” that “397 children formerly associated with armed forces and groups have benefited from reintegration services,” and that more than “700 officers of the defence and security forces have been trained” in human rights.

a4918.speaker: Virginia Gamba, Special Representative of the UN Secretary-General for Children and Armed Conflict
a4918.speech: Warns that “the continued deterioration of the security situation has particularly affected children's access to education, with more than 800,000 children affected by school closures” ; calls for the “full implementation” of the commitments made, urging the Burkinabè government to guarantee accountability and to ensure access to justice and reparations for child victims, and appeals to donors to fund reintegration programmes.

a4947.speaker: Residents in Sitsatsaweni
a4947.speech: Have reported a rise in copper cable theft since the load shedding began.

a4947.speaker: Comfort Mdluli, a resident of Sitsatsaweni
a4947.speech: Said several homesteads were left without electricity for days after thieves stole cables from poles, mainly during evening outages: "We had a number of homesteads and a shop left without electricity last week after thieves cut off electricity cables from the poles."

a4947.speaker: Kaizer Mathonsi, leader of the Lugongolweni community police
a4947.speech: Confirmed they are reinforcing strategies to curb the crime wave, especially during evening blackouts: "We are aware of criminals taking advantage of the dark hours, and our members are working to counter these criminal activities."

a4947.speaker: Kaizer Mathonsi, leader of the Lugongolweni community police
a4947.speech: Lamented the lack of basic equipment such as torches and whistles, which are essential for night patrols and alerting fellow community officers.

a4947.speaker: Kaizer Mathonsi, leader of the Lugongolweni community police
a4947.speech: Advised small business owners to properly secure their premises at night or consider hiring private security guards: "Some shops are left unattended overnight, making them easy targets for criminals," he warned.

a4992.speaker: United Nations Food and Agriculture Organization (FAO) and Intergovernmental Authority on Development (IGAD) (joint report)
a4992.speech: Said that more than 88 million people in East and Central Africa faced food insecurity and required urgent humanitarian assistance in June 2025, of whom 57.1 million were in seven of the eight IGAD member states, namely Djibouti, Ethiopia, Kenya, Somalia, South Sudan, Sudan, and Uganda: "Levels of acute food insecurity across the region remained concerning, with ongoing or approaching lean seasons compounding the effects of conflict, climatic shocks, and macroeconomic challenges in many countries." ; The two organisations noted that countries battling conflict are the worst affected as the crises continue to disrupt livelihoods and undermine food security across the region, including Ethiopia, Somalia, South Sudan, Sudan, and the Democratic Republic of the Congo, with the last three being the worst affected.

a4992.speaker: United Nations Food and Agriculture Organization (FAO) and Intergovernmental Authority on Development (IGAD)
a4992.speech: Said an estimated 23.8 million people had been forcibly displaced across the region as of the end of June, including 18 million internally displaced persons and 5.8 million refugees and asylum seekers; they observed that conflict, insecurity, and climatic shocks remained the primary drivers of displacement, and that Sudan accounted for over half of the region's total IDPs, at 10.1 million, 2.4 million displaced before the start of the ongoing conflict, and 7.7 million after.

a5005.speaker: Pamela Fessenden, Mission Director for the US Agency for International Development (USAID) in Malawi
a5005.speech: Highlighted the importance of civil society in holding leaders accountable and promoting democracy: “The role of civil society will be even more critical in ensuring that Parliament is responsive, elections are free and fair, and every citizen’s voice is heard” ; “Today’s handover is more than just providing a vehicle and equipment. It’s an investment in mobility, access, and visibility, so you can reach remote areas faster and hold leaders accountable.”

a5005.speaker: Willy Kambwandira, Executive Director of the Centre for Social Accountability and Transparency (CSAT)
a5005.speech: Welcomed the support, describing the donation as an investment in their work: “This donation will enable us to reach more people and promote accountability and transparency in governance.”

a5056.speaker: United Nations Children's Fund (UNICEF) (report)
a5056.speech: Estimates that around 3.4 million children require humanitarian assistance in Mozambique, highlighting the need for an additional $35.6 million (€31.1 million) in funding; states that the crisis in Mozambique results from armed insecurity in the north of the country and the cholera outbreak that mainly affects the province of Nampula ; “The security situation in the north remains volatile, with several incidents reported in Cabo Delgado and Niassa forcing children and families out of their homes.”

a5056.speaker: United Nations Children's Fund (UNICEF)
a5056.speech: Reports that by May, health workers had vaccinated around 2.3 million people against cholera in the country, and they had screened 357,500 children for malnutrition, of whom almost 12,600 received “life-saving treatment”; that during the same period it provided drinking water to 116,900 children and families, 149,500 children and caregivers received psychosocial support, and 173,300 children had access to education.

a5056.speaker: United Nations Children's Fund (UNICEF)
a5056.speech: “UNICEF HAC Appeal [Humanitarian Action for Children Appeal] 2025 has a funding gap of USD 35.6 million” ; warns that, with funding shortages, at least two million children need “critical vaccination”, 572,800 children and families require safe drinking water, 335,500 people need psychosocial support, and “children with severe acute malnutrition will not survive without the treatment they need”.

a5114.speaker: Doreen Robinson, USAID senior regional environment adviser
a5114.speech: "Introducing adaptation concepts to communities can be challenging." ; "We live in a world with so much information, and where the climate change message is often too technical, complicated and easily influenced by the cultural, social and political environment. USAID is committed to breaking these barriers to get good, relevant, understandable and timely climate information to people to help them change their lives for the better."

a5114.speaker: Farmers (initial testimonies)
a5114.speech: Initial testimonies from farmers indicate exciting opportunities to scale out the climate-smart community model in a number of communities in different regions.

a5184.speaker: Norwegian Refugee Council
a5184.speech: Calls for a quadrupling of the current support, to ensure affected communities in DR Congo receive immediate aid.

a5184.speaker: Jan Egeland, Secretary General of the Norwegian Refugee Council
a5184.speech: “We cannot afford the pledging conference to be an ‘all talk and no action’ kind of event. The international community needs to wake up. Today, the lack of funds is already affecting humanitarian operations. Our teams in North Kivu have seen peer agencies pulling out or scaling down, while the needs are increasing.” ; “The stakes are incredibly high in DR Congo. Continued inaction would be measured in loss of civilian lives.”

a5285.speaker: Samia Suluhu Hassan, President of Tanzania
a5285.speech: Emphasised that the bridge not only connects Mwanza and Geita regions but also integrates the entire Great Lakes region, creating new social and economic opportunities; she said the bridge symbolises the government's ability to execute major development projects and its commitment to national growth.

a5285.speaker: Samia Suluhu Hassan, President of Tanzania
a5285.speech: "This bridge is a national landmark and a testament to our progress. It confirms that Tanzania is becoming a strong economic nation, capable of designing, executing and completing large-scale development projects independently," said President Samia, urging security agencies to protect the national asset.

a5285.speaker: Samia Suluhu Hassan, President of Tanzania
a5285.speech: Highlighted that the bridge's completion would reduce transport costs, enhance market access and alleviate the travel difficulties previously experienced by Lake Zone residents; she acknowledged the previous noise and criticisms surrounding the project but reaffirmed her resolve to see through President Magufuli's vision to completion, and noted that the bridge illustrates Tanzania's economic maturity and self-reliance in planning and financing its development initiatives without foreign aid.

a5285.speaker: Abdallah Ulega, Minister for Works
a5285.speech: Praised President Samia for her consistent oversight and commitment to the project, recalled her 2020 campaign promise to complete strategic infrastructure projects including this bridge, the Standard Gauge Railway and the Julius Nyerere Hydropower Dam, and stated that when President Samia took office the project was only 25 per cent complete and had received just 152bn/- in payments, while by completion the government had disbursed over 450bn/-: "That's why we say, Madam President, you have delivered. You are a good shepherd. You fulfilled all your promises and this bridge is a national symbol of independent decision-making," adding that her policy of continuing all strategic projects initiated by her predecessor had proven true.

a5285.speaker: Kassim Majaliwa, Prime Minister of Tanzania
a5285.speech: Praised the President's commitment to timely delivery of strategic projects which now are going to boost the country's economy.

a5285.speaker: Stephen Wassira, CCM Vice-Chairperson for Mainland Tanzania
a5285.speech: Echoed that message, calling the bridge proof that development pledges by the CCM are implemented.

a5285.speaker: Said Mtanda, Mwanza Regional Commissioner
a5285.speech: Expressed gratitude for the 5.6tr/- allocated to Mwanza region over the past four years for strategic development, including the JP Magufuli Bridge, which is expected to significantly boost the region's and the nation's economy.

a5285.speaker: Engineer Paschal Ambrose, TANROADS Mwanza Regional Manager
a5285.speech: Said the bridge was designed using "extradosed" long-span bridge technology featuring three main pylons, each 40 metres high and spaced 150 metres apart; that in total the bridge is supported by 67 pillars, with 64 installed along the span; that each pillar is anchored by foundation piles drilled between 15.5 and 66 metres deep into Lake Victoria's bed; that the bridge includes a dual carriageway with seven-metre lanes in each direction and 2.5-metre shoulders; and that the total length of the connecting roads is 1,650 metres, with road markings and safety signs installed to ensure the safety of all users.

a5337.speaker: Themba Chirwa, MCA Director for Increase and Productivity Project
a5337.speech: Said the agreement was premised on establishing policies that would help councils collect taxes and use them effectively, and that the project also included a property mapping and evaluation process to help councils have accurate information on properties in areas under their jurisdiction ; "The main objective of this agreement is to support councils in establishing policies and systems that will help them collect taxes and use them effectively."

a5337.speaker: Esther Sagawa, Malga (Malawi Local Government Association) President
a5337.speech: Urged the councils to use the funds provided wisely ; "We are grateful for this support and will ensure that the funds are used effectively to benefit service users."

a5337.speaker: Archangel Bakolo, Zomba City Chief Executive Officer
a5337.speech: Said the councils would ensure that the funds were used effectively to support development projects in their areas ; "We will make sure that the funds are used transparently and accountably to benefit residents."

a5407.speaker: Nigerian federal government
a5407.speech: Unveiled a new strategy to reduce Nigeria's over-reliance on international donors for healthcare, pledging to increase domestic funding and boost local manufacturing of essential medicines and medical supplies; the plan was announced on Monday at the HIV/AIDS, Tuberculosis and Malaria Generative Workshop in Abuja.

a5407.speaker: Muhammad Pate, Coordinating Minister of Health and Social Welfare
a5407.speech: Stressed that Nigeria must urgently take ownership of financing its health system and warned that reliance on foreign aid is unsustainable; said that for more than two decades the country has benefited from the generosity of external partners in the fight against HIV, malaria and other conditions: "These partnerships have supported our response to disease burdens, expanded access to services, and strengthened our health system" ; pointed out that the recent suspension of some of the World Health Organisation's funding proves the need to build stronger country-led systems, strengthen local institutions, and take full control of programme management; added that the existing global health financing structure, shaped over the past 25 years, has proved inadequate in addressing Nigeria's health challenges.

a5407.speaker: Muhammad Pate, Coordinating Minister of Health and Social Welfare
a5407.speech: Urged state governments to take greater responsibility for the health of their residents and commit a portion of their increased revenues to healthcare; said the administration will raise health budget allocations at both national and state levels, ensure timely release of funds, retain donor-funded health workers, and boost local manufacturing of medicines and medical supplies; added that recommendations from the workshop would feed into ongoing reforms and a sector-wide approach already agreed with state governments.

a5407.speaker: Temitope Ilori, Director General of the National Agency for the Control of AIDS (NACA)
a5407.speech: Explained that the workshop aimed to identify immediate gaps and develop long-term sustainability plans to ensure Nigeria is not overly dependent on foreign aid; said the focus is on Nigeria taking ownership of its health response, covering HIV, TB, malaria, maternal and child health, through government structures, domestic resource mobilisation and uninterrupted service delivery ; "We have the political will. This administration is a listening administration and has facilitated resources to ensure no gaps in service delivery" ; "Because of that political will, we will have the necessary resources to sustain locally driven health programmes."

a5421.speaker: Esther Lukhere, 57, maize mill owner in Samuel Chakwira Village, Mzimba
a5421.speech: “In my life, I have always had an ambition to own a maize mill, but I had no capital. My dream was fuelled by long walks to the nearest maize mill, which was about 12 kilometres away.” ; “I joined the initiative in 2023 in Thundwe Catchment Area. I received K48 000 after working for a 24-day cycle. This birthed the maize mill business.” ; “I invested part of the money in a savings and loans group [SLG], where I later borrowed K150 000. I moulded bricks, which I sold for K550 000.” ; “After selling the bricks, I repaid the loan at K240 000, including interest. The remainder was enough for the maize inlet of the grinding mill, boots, diesel and cement for my dream business.”

a5421.speaker: Tionge Mkandawire, from Chinthechi Village
a5421.speech: “We feel relieved. At last, we no longer struggle to mill our maize.”

a5421.speaker: Solomon, son of Esther Lukhere who runs the maize mill business
a5421.speech: “Now we can afford fertiliser, food and some farm workers from the proceeds of the maize mill. We plan to construct a brick house for the maize mill.”

a5421.speaker: Olive Nyalira, desk officer for the government project
a5421.speech: Says success stories like Lukhere’s show that the initiative is addressing poverty among participants: “Lukhere could be a symbol of success achieved by many beneficiaries in Mzimba. Some people have constructed houses by using the earnings from the climate-smart programme wisely.”

a5421.speaker: Richard Chapweteka, National Local Government Finance Committee board chairperson
a5421.speech: Says it is pleasing that success stories are on the increase after several years of focused social protection programme: “People’s livelihoods are being transformed and there is progressive livelihood transformation as households move from poverty to self-sustenance and well-being.”

a5567.speaker: Abdi Mahamoud Eybe, Ambassador of the Republic of Djibouti to Ethiopia and Permanent Representative to the African Union and the ECA
a5567.speech: On the purpose of the President's state visit to Ethiopia: said the visit is part of the regular contacts that exist between the leaders of the two countries and that its purpose is to raise the quality of their relations to an ever higher level; recalled that the two countries have had ancestral, solid and fraternal relations since time immemorial, that sustained growth born two decades ago required the modernisation of port, maritime and communication infrastructure linking Djibouti and Ethiopia, and that together they launched an exemplary regional integration programme which facilitated trade, boosted the economies and combated poverty, a model relationship that remains an example for the whole continent.

a5567.speaker: Abdi Mahamoud Eybe, Ambassador of the Republic of Djibouti to Ethiopia
a5567.speech: On the welcome and schedule of the visit: said that on arrival the President received a very warm, high-level welcome from the Ethiopian leader, that Prime Minister Dr Abiy was surrounded by several members of his government including the Minister of Economy and Finance, Ahmed Chideh, a welcome that perfectly reflects the solidity and quality of relations between the two countries; said that during his stay in Addis Ababa the President held a one-on-one meeting with Ethiopian Prime Minister Dr Abiy Ahmed, followed by a bilateral meeting between the two countries' delegations to further improve trade and the interconnection unique in Africa that exists between Djibouti and Ethiopia.

a5567.speaker: Abdi Mahamoud Eybe, Ambassador of the Republic of Djibouti to Ethiopia
a5567.speech: On regional instability and the civil war: said that thanks to the nationalism, wisdom, honesty and will for peace of its Prime Minister, Ethiopia is about to settle this conflict which no country could desire or wish for; recalled that since the beginning of this fratricidal war the Republic of Djibouti, through its President, never hesitated to support the Ethiopian government and help it overcome its tragic ordeal, and that the Prime Minister's firmness triggered great hope because the country is today on the final path to peace, a true and lasting peace.

a5567.speaker: Abdi Mahamoud Eybe, Permanent Representative of Djibouti to the African Union
a5567.speech: On Djibouti's weight within the African Union: recalled that Djibouti began to play a leading role so that the region could enjoy lasting peace and establish stability favourable to its socio-economic development; that the country was barely ten years old when it successfully mediated between Ethiopia and Somalia and that, thanks to its neutrality, Djiboutian diplomacy achieved remarkable feats; said Djibouti has taken part in all peace missions in Africa and elsewhere and has chaired the AU Peace and Security Council more than any other member: "we are the only country to have been re-elected for a third consecutive time within this council", concluding that the country holds a privileged position and is doing very well in terms of diplomatic weight.

a5567.speaker: Abdi Mahamoud Eybe, Permanent Representative of Djibouti to the African Union
a5567.speech: On the African Union ending AMISOM's mandate: said there is no withdrawal whatsoever on the part of the African Union; that if the AMISOM mission ends it gives way to a new, time-limited mission whose objective is to strengthen the capacities of all the structures of the Somali state, whether civilian or military, so as to allow the country to take charge of itself, have proper institutional functioning and ensure its own security; that unlike AMISOM this new mission, called ATMIS, is a transition mission intended to prepare the country to stand on its own, and that in addition to the African Union forces already in place ATMIS will deploy teams of technocrats to train and put in place a solid, functional and viable state structure, with the transition period expected to last two years.

a5567.speaker: Abdi Mahamoud Eybe, Permanent Representative of Djibouti to the African Union
a5567.speech: On whether the two-year mandate is renewable: said ATMIS's mandate will officially end at the end of 2024, but that no one knows what the future holds and everything will depend on the situation on the ground and on the success of this new mission.

a5567.speaker: Abdi Mahamoud Eybe, Permanent Representative of Djibouti to the African Union
a5567.speech: On whether the UN Security Council validated the mission: "Absolutely!" said the African Union has always worked in close collaboration with the United Nations Security Council and that the objective of both organisations is to move things forward in Somalia in the interest of the Somali people; ATMIS will not only improve the capacities of the Somali security forces to confront and effectively fight the Al-Shabaab terrorists, but will also develop the administrative structures of the state and make them very effective, the objective being to enable Somalia to take charge of itself and ensure the country's stability and security.

a5578.speaker: MpD (Movement for Democracy party, political declaration delivered by MP Emanuel Barbosa)
a5578.speech: Criticised what it considers to be “unfounded statements” about the protocol, accusing certain sectors of society of “shamefully exploiting national sentiment”.

a5578.speaker: MpD (Movement for Democracy party)
a5578.speech: “With the Protocol, out of the 30,000 tonnes of our potential, we allow the catching of 7,000 tonnes, but we have a financial counterpart that feeds the Autonomous Fisheries Fund, finances programmes in Cape Verde’s coastal areas, allows Cape Verdean fishermen to embark on European vessels and involves the scientific community” ; stressed that the total financial compensation under the agreement, set at 3.9 million euros, is applied to strengthening the monitoring, control and surveillance of fishing activities, to scientific research on fishery resources, to the sanitary control of fishery products and to support for coastal communities, with particular attention to the training and employability of women and young people.

a5578.speaker: Emanuel Barbosa, MpD Member of Parliament
a5578.speech: “Without the agreement, we have neither fish nor money.”

a5578.speaker: MpD (Movement for Democracy party)
a5578.speech: Recalled that this protocol stems from the fisheries partnership agreement signed between Cape Verde and the European Union on 12 February 2007, during the PAICV’s term in office ; “It can therefore easily be deduced that the PAICV supports this protocol and should help to inform the less well-informed members of our society.”

a5578.speaker: MpD (Movement for Democracy party)
a5578.speech: Assures that the Government intends to foster economic and business partnerships with the Cape Verdean private sector, in order to increase domestic catches and encourage the landing of catches in the archipelago ; “This will provide returns in processing, trucking, packaging, stevedoring and increased exports from Cape Verde.”

a5613.speaker: Prince Moye, Liberian Senate Committee Chair on Ways, Means, Finance, and Budget (Bong County Senator)
a5613.speech: said at a press conference on Tuesday, September 9, 2025, in Monrovia: “The amount was discovered based on the innovation of the Liberian Senate to investigate storage fees at the LPRC” ; said the amount expected to be raised annually will go towards social programs amid the USAID drawdown.

a5613.speaker: Prince Moye, Liberian Senate Committee Chair on Ways, Means, Finance, and Budget
a5613.speech: thanked President Joseph Boakai for endorsing the report and allowing the National Legislature to work independently.

a5622.speaker: Akatswiri Holdings
a5622.speech: Has committed to minimizing ecological damage through Environmental and Social Impact Assessments (ESIA) to ensure sustainable operations; reforestation and land reclamation to preserve Mulanje Mountain's biodiversity; and integration of renewable energy solutions to reduce the carbon footprint of the mining process.

a5622.speaker: Hilton Banda, Managing Director of Akatswiri Holdings
a5622.speech: "This project is about more than mining—it's about building a brighter, self-reliant future for Malawi."

a5633.speaker: Somali Ministry of Foreign Affairs and International Cooperation (press statement, October 9, 2025)
a5633.speech: Expressed the Federal Republic of Somalia's profound appreciation for the recent peace agreement reached in Sharm El-Sheikh, Egypt, which aims to end the devastating two-year conflict in the Gaza Strip, welcoming the deal as a major step toward a just and comprehensive resolution of the Palestinian cause.

a5633.speaker: Somali Ministry of Foreign Affairs and International Cooperation (press statement)
a5633.speech: Reiterated Somalia's steadfast support for the legitimate rights of the Palestinian people, foremost among them the right to establish an independent and sovereign state with Jerusalem as its capital.

a5633.speaker: Somali government
a5633.speech: Hopes that this agreement will serve as a genuine step toward ending the suffering of the Palestinian people and consolidating security and stability in the wider region, and expressed its full support for all efforts aimed at protecting human dignity, reinforcing respect for international law, and advancing a just and comprehensive resolution to the Palestinian cause.

a5687.speaker: Ministry of the Interior of Niger (decision)
a5687.speech: Issued the decision ordering the closure of two NGOs, amid a broader review of NGO operations in the country.

a5687.speaker: National Council for the Safeguarding of the Fatherland (Niger)
a5687.speech: The move is part of its efforts to align NGO activities with national priorities and ensure compliance with regulatory frameworks; other NGOs, such as Plan International and the Hanns Seidel Foundation, have also been called in for discussions to ensure their operations align with the government's guidelines.

a5808.speaker: Prof. Sidikou Ramatou Djermakoye Seyni, Minister of Population, Social Action and National Solidarity (Niger)
a5808.speech: stated that the project had made it possible to assist 6,461 vulnerable households with cash and food, to build 19 water points, to distribute non-food, hygiene and dignity kits to 1,500 households, to build 48 emergency and VIP double-cabin latrines, to screen 7,100 children under five, to distribute fortified flour to 2,000 children under five and 2,000 pregnant and breastfeeding women, to support the early warning system, to facilitate the dissemination of information on agricultural product prices and to support the holding of several humanitarian coordination forums.

a5808.speaker: Prof. Sidikou Ramatou Djermakoye Seyni, Minister of Population, Social Action and National Solidarity (Niger)
a5808.speech: explained that these results were achieved thanks to good and frank collaboration among several actors, despite the difficult situation facing not only the humanitarian world through the dwindling of funding, but also the difficult access affecting the various intervention zones, in particular the Tillabéri region ; “We extend our warm thanks to all those actors who worked for the success of this project, beginning with the President of the Republic, Head of State, Army General Abdourahamane Tiani, and the Prime Minister, Minister of the Economy and Finance, Mr Ali Mahaman Lamine Zeine, who, through their policy, have always supported every action aimed at improving the well-being of the population.”

a5808.speaker: Claudia Sessouma, Country Director of the Welthungerhilfe project
a5808.speech: recalled that her organisation, created in 1962, is one of the largest German NGOs working in development cooperation and humanitarian aid; the project claims political and religious neutrality and works in food and nutrition security, water-hygiene-sanitation, basic education, and economic and rural development in Africa, Asia and Latin America, and is committed to a duty of accountability towards communities, donors and authorities at all levels ; indicated that in Niger the project has been implemented since July 2023 and is funded to the tune of 4.3 million euros ; “As a humanitarian project, it responds to the urgent needs of vulnerable households, in particular displaced persons and the host communities that receive them.”

a5812.speaker: Lesotho Judiciary strategic plan (mission statement)
a5812.speech: Its mission was declared as, “to have an independent, effective and transparent judiciary in the administration of Justice.”

a5812.speaker: Administration of the Judiciary Act, 2011 (preamble)
a5812.speech: proclaimed: “to provide for an autonomous and accountable system of the Judiciary”. One of the key objectives was outlined as the effective and timely disposal of cases.

a5812.speaker: Acting Chief Justice Monaphathi, Lesotho Judiciary (Practice Directive No 1/01 of 2014)
a5812.speech: issued a Practice Directive No 1/01 of 2014, which introduced the operation of the Individual Docket System in order to make the Lesotho Judicial system judge owned and driven from allocation to disposition.

a5812.speaker: Chief Justice Nthomeng Majara (Practice Directive No 1 of 2016 and High Court (Amendment) Rules, 2016)
a5812.speech: issued Practice Directive No 1 of 2016 which ensured the courts' readiness for every case that has been set down for hearing and to have all pleadings and documents in their proper order; that directive further restricted postponements of cases and ensured authenticity of court orders. In the same year, she made the High Court (Amendment) Rules, 2016, which, inter alia, introduced the maiden pre-trial procedures.

a5812.speaker: Chief Justice Sakoane (Superior Practice Directive No 2 of 2021)
a5812.speech: promulgated the Superior Practice Directive No 2, which facilitated the use of technology in the mist of the Covid pandemic and changed the level field in terms of checklists to be followed in ensuring that cases are ready for hearing when brought before the courts.

a5921.speaker: Council of Ministers of Côte d'Ivoire (report on the country's participation in the IMF/World Bank Annual Meetings)
a5921.speech: Took note, on 30 October 2024, of the report on Côte d'Ivoire's participation in the Annual Meetings of the World Bank Group and the International Monetary Fund (IMF) held from 21 to 26 October 2024, noting that the Ivorian delegation was led by the Minister of Economy, Planning and Development in collaboration with the Ministry of Finance and Budget, and that the meetings highlighted crucial issues for Africa's economic resilience and transformation, including the creation of a third African chair on the IMF Board.

a5921.speaker: Officials of the IMF, the World Bank Group and private-sector actors
a5921.speech: Praised Côte d'Ivoire's national economic performance, all underlining the country's remarkable progress in terms of growth and stability.

a6095.speaker: Samreen Hussain, MSF medical coordinator in Ethiopia
a6095.speech: "Current cholera outbreaks in the Horn of Africa are among the longest outbreaks ever recorded in the region and there are multiple outbreaks happening at the same time. While we are putting an end to one outbreak in one location, a new outbreak starts elsewhere."

a6095.speaker: Kelly Khabala, deputy medical coordinator of MSF's work in Kenya
a6095.speech: Without clean water and decent sanitation, these efforts are in vain, says Kelly Khabala. "Despite coordinated health promotion activities and a cholera vaccination campaign done in February 2023, this outbreak cannot be controlled without the prioritisation of resources towards sustained preventative water, sanitation and hygiene interventions."

a6095.speaker: Kelly Khabala, deputy medical coordinator of MSF's work in Kenya
a6095.speech: "If sanitation is not improved in quality and scale, other epidemics, such as hepatitis E, will erupt in the camps at Dadaab. This would particularly impact new arrivals and some of the older refugees in the blocks who have no access to latrines."

a6095.speaker: Mohamed Abdiwahab Omar, MSF nursing activity manager
a6095.speech: describes his journey to reach a remote community in the Somali region of Ethiopia where a lethal combination of cholera and malnutrition had caused a number of recent deaths. "In a convoy of four 4x4 vehicles, we set off from our project office in Jijiga towards Dawa zone, on the border with Kenya. For seven days we drove on dirt roads lined with animal carcasses through the drought-stricken region. On day three, heavy rains unleashed widespread flooding; roads and bridges were washed away, forcing us to find alternative routes. Our cars got repeatedly stuck in mud while attempting to cross riverbeds and had to be towed out, while the passengers had to alight and cross on foot to make the cars less heavy. We only made it there safely thanks to our skillful drivers."

a6095.speaker: MSF (Medecins Sans Frontieres)
a6095.speech: Today, MSF calls for urgent action to be taken to improve people's access to clean water and decent sanitation. It is critical that action is taken now to reduce the burden of cholera, both within the Horn of Africa and globally, before the death toll from this preventable disease rises even further.

a6095.speaker: International donors (May 2023 pledges)
a6095.speech: In May 2023, international donors pledged just US$2.4 billion of the US$7 billion required for humanitarian assistance for people in the Horn of Africa affected by drought and conflict.

a6125.speaker: Hopeson Chatala, 25, enumerator from Chipakuza Village, Chikwawa District (CRS Rapid Feedback Monitoring System project)
a6125.speech: “Connecting with people 24/7 opens numerous opportunities in my life.” ; “I’m glad to be useful to my community. With high illiteracy, you need someone who can translate the information to a language many people understand.” ; “This is the primary use of this smartphone; it gives my community the information we need the most to survive, but the benefits go beyond the project. It has transformed my life and skills. Thanks to my experience and skills as an enumerator, I got a six-month contract with Illovo Sugar Malawi plc as a data entry clerk.” ; “I no longer live with my mother. I graduated from that,” he brags.

a6169.speaker: Dr Rudie van Vuuren, N/a’an ku sê Foundation
a6169.speech: “It is time for the Namibian government to become self-sustainable and no longer rely on donors,” said in an interview with Network Media Hub (NMH) last week.

a6169.speaker: Kelsey Prediger, founder of the Pangolin Conservation and Research Foundation
a6169.speech: According to Prediger, the US government had supported their efforts against pangolin traffickers, “but now everything is indefinitely frozen.”

a6290.speaker: Somalia Disaster Management Agency (SoDMA)
a6290.speech: According to SoDMA, more than 1.7 million people were affected by the heavy rains and floods that hit Somalia in late 2023, displacing hundreds of thousands and destroying crops and infrastructure.

a6290.speaker: Somalia Disaster Management Agency (SoDMA)
a6290.speech: The agency said it is working to enhance the resilience and capacity of the communities to cope with the impacts of climate change and natural disasters.

a6290.speaker: Somalia Disaster Management Agency (SoDMA)
a6290.speech: Said it will continue to monitor the weather situation and provide updates and assistance to the affected populations ; the agency also appealed for more funding and resources from the international community to address the humanitarian needs and challenges in Somalia.

a6290.speaker: Ali Gudlawe Hussein, President of Hirshabelle State
a6290.speech: Thanked the delegation for their visit and expressed his appreciation for the support and cooperation of SoDMA. He also urged the residents of Jowhar and other flood-prone areas to follow the guidelines and warnings issued by the agency and the authorities.

a6302.speaker: Stakeholders
a6302.speech: Complain about the delay to approve the law by the Ministry of Justice.

a6302.speaker: Bereket Tesfaye, advisor at the German Corporation for International Cooperation (GIZ)
a6302.speech: Stated that regulatory authorities are not doing enough.

a6302.speaker: Addisu Tibebu, environmental regulation lead at the Environmental Protection Authority (EPA)
a6302.speech: Stated that the agency is working to create awareness while awaiting the directive's approval by MoJ.

a6302.speaker: World Health Organization (WHO)
a6302.speech: According to WHO, high levels of lead exposure can severely damage the brain and central nervous system, potentially leading to coma, convulsions, or death, and young children are vulnerable as they absorb four to five times more lead than adults ; WHO estimates that lead exposure resulted in 1.5 million deaths in 2021, primarily from cardiovascular effects, with one in three children being exposed, and that it causes a loss of 98.2 million IQ points annually in Africa, resulting in economic losses of 134.7 billion dollars.

a6302.speaker: Meles Solomon, head of the Ministry of Health's infant and children health desk
a6302.speech: Stated lead exposure was given little attention as the government's focus has been on infectious diseases ; said that improper lead waste disposal has caused serious health risks.

a6302.speaker: Tadesse Amera (PhD), executive director of PAN Ethiopia
a6302.speech: Said that EPA needs capable personnel to regulate and control lead exposure ; according to Tadesse, discarded car batteries, aging water pipes, and lead-contaminated cookware pose severe health threats, and lead poisoning is irreversible: "The workers will wake up once they know the effect," he told Fortune, referring to battery recycling hands. "The directive is expected to improve worker safety." He recommends public awareness, focus on prevention, and safety measures for workers involved in battery recycling ; according to Tadesse, Ethiopia receives a large amount of recycled batteries.

a6302.speaker: Field assessments conducted by EPA and GIZ in June 2022
a6302.speech: Found out that lead exposure contributed to serious health and environmental risks; they uncovered that scrap metals that contain lead were being recycled into household utensils, and that plates made with lead alloys and large cooking pots used by community organizations like Iddir were found to contain lead.

a6302.speaker: Suleiman Idris, a recycler from Ayene Tsige Recycling Factory
a6302.speech: Said that his business's survival depends on the implementation of the EPR system ; says that there would not be sufficient lead battery supply for recycling, giving way to illegal scrapping and smuggling, if the government does not implement the strict rules soon.

a6302.speaker: Argaw Ambelu (Prof), environmental health expert
a6302.speech: Conducted research in Jimma and Addis Abeba, finding lead levels in air and water exceeding WHO recommendations; he believes that lead poisoning is causing diseases like kidney failure. "It is a silent killer," he said. "Its effect on health is not well studied." Everyday items such as coffee cups, food colorings, and children's toys are commonly contaminated with lead, according to him.

a6694.speaker: United Nations
a6694.speech: Estimates that $1.8 billion in immediate humanitarian aid is needed for South Sudan, Yemen, Somalia and Nigeria.

a6694.speaker: Oxfam
a6694.speech: Attributes this to the fact that the government was better prepared to deliver food and water to millions.

a6694.speaker: Alex de Waal, British author and Africa researcher
a6694.speech: "Politics creates famine, and politics can stop it."

a6694.speaker: Trump administration (proposed foreign aid budget)
a6694.speech: Recommends deep funding cuts to global food security programs, while global food security initiatives enjoy bipartisan support in the US Congress.

a6694.speaker: One Acre Fund (Stephanie Hanson and Whitney McFerron)
a6694.speech: As our organization is currently demonstrating in six African countries, farmers can build their asset bases with training and financial support ; we believe African governments and bilateral donors should deepen their investments in programs that provide farmers with the skills to produce long-term crops, especially trees, sustainably.

a6974.speaker: Rubber Processors Association of Ghana (RUPAG) (press statement)
a6974.speech: Issued a statement confirming The Chronicle's story and demanding an urgent crackdown on what it describes as illegal raw rubber exports ; stated categorically that unregulated exports threaten Ghana's 24-Hour economy, jobs and industrialization agenda ; called on security agencies to intervene in the illegal and unregulated export of raw rubber (cuplumps), which continues to undermine Ghana's rubber value addition agenda and broader industrialization goals ; said the ongoing smuggling of raw cup lumps directly contravenes the Tree Crops Development Authority's ban under the Tree Crops Regulations, 2023 (L.I.2471), and severely threatens the survival of local processing companies and thousands of livelihoods ; "Our factories have the capacity and expertise to process all locally produced rubber. However, ongoing illegal exports deny us access to raw materials, putting processing plants, investments, and jobs at serious risk."

a6974.speaker: Rubber Processors Association of Ghana (RUPAG) (press statement)
a6974.speech: Said exporting raw cuplumps directly contradicts the government's industrialization strategy, particularly the 24-hour economy agenda, and drains Ghana of potential foreign exchange, stifles industrial development and weakens supply to local factories ; said that contrary to fears that halting raw exports may cause job losses, enforcing local processing before export leads to more jobs across the entire value chain, and "Stopping raw exports is not a loss; it is a necessary lever for job creation, expansion, and long-term national prosperity" ; said exports threaten over 1,300 direct jobs and more than 70,000 indirect livelihoods across Ghana's rubber sector, that the Rubber Outgrower Plantation Project supporting over 11,800 farmers on 55,599 hectares faces serious disruption as illegal buyers lure farmers away from formal processing channels, and that the situation is particularly alarming for the recovery of over GHS 450,000,000.00 in credit financing extended to the sector.

a6974.speaker: Rubber Processors Association of Ghana (RUPAG) (press statement)
a6974.speech: Said that although the TCDA introduced a permit system in April 2025 to control exports, smugglers reportedly bypass the rules, destabilizing the market, in breach of Act 1010 and the Tree Crops Regulations, 2023 (L.I. 2471) ; appealed to the Ghana Police Service, National Security, Customs Division of the Ghana Revenue Authority, National Investigations Bureau (NIB) and the Economic and Organized Crime Office (EOCO) to strengthen surveillance at all export points, intercept illicit shipments and prosecute offenders in accordance with the law ; urged government and industry stakeholders to deepen public-private partnerships to protect agribusiness investments, boost domestic processing and ensure the rubber sector drives Ghana's economic transformation under the 24-hour economy vision.

a6974.speaker: Andrew Okrah, Chief Executive Officer of Tree Crop Development Authority (TCDA)
a6974.speech: Told The Chronicle that loading of rubber from one jurisdiction to another could not be referred to as illegal exports of raw rubber.

a7142.speaker: Benjamin Netanyahu, Israeli Prime Minister
a7142.speech: Announced on Tuesday that Israel will allow the inhabitants of the Gaza Strip who wish to flee the Palestinian territory to leave for abroad, appealing in an interview with i24 News: "In Syria, millions left (...), in Ukraine, millions left, in Afghanistan, millions left... And suddenly they [the international community] decide that, in Gaza, civilians must remain trapped? Give them the opportunity to leave, first of all, the combat zones and, in general, the territory, if that is what they wish." ; noting that he could not go into details, reported that he is in contact with various countries as possible hosts, insisting that "the most natural thing, for all those who speak out, those who say they care about the Palestinians and want to help them, is to open their doors" to anyone who wants to leave the territory ; "We are going to allow that, first of all, within Gaza, during the fighting, and we will certainly also allow them to leave Gaza. We are not expelling them, but we are allowing them to leave, and that is what is happening."

a7142.speaker: Benjamin Netanyahu, Israeli Prime Minister
a7142.speech: Rejected the possibility of a 60-day ceasefire with Hamas: "I think we have already gone beyond that. We tried, we made all kinds of attempts (...), but in the end they were just deceiving us," referring to the previous rounds, which produced no results ; reiterated that he wants to recover all of the roughly 50 hostages held by Hamas, of whom an estimated 20 are alive.

a7142.speaker: Israeli Army
a7142.speech: Announced a new phase of the fighting, after 22 months of offensive, following the Security Cabinet's approval of the plan to occupy Gaza City and displace hundreds of thousands of its inhabitants, in addition to the expansion of military operations to the refugee camps on the enclave's central coast.

a7142.speaker: International press (cited)
a7142.speech: According to the international press, in addition to the occupation of Gaza City, the new Israeli plan, which has drawn wide criticism inside and outside Israel, has as its objectives the destruction of the Palestinian armed group and the release of the hostages, followed by the creation of a "security perimeter" and the handover of the territory to a civil administration that is not hostile to Tel Aviv.

a7142.speaker: Badr Abdelaty, Egypt's Minister of Foreign Affairs
a7142.speech: Revealed to journalists in Cairo that his country is in negotiations with Hamas and Israel to revive the ceasefire proposal of the US envoy to the Middle East, Steve Witkoff, with whom he says he maintains "daily contact".

a7142.speaker: United Nations (UN)
a7142.speech: According to the UN, the Gaza Strip, totally dependent on humanitarian aid, is threatened by "widespread famine"; the UN has called for the entry of urgent support in the face of an "unimaginable catastrophe".

a7142.speaker: Israel
a7142.speech: Denies this warning of widespread famine.

a7142.speaker: Local authorities (Gaza)
a7142.speech: According to local authorities, the Israeli military operation has already caused more than 61,000 deaths.

a7227.speaker: Kutloano Pheko, Principal Information Officer of the Ministry of Foreign Affairs and International Relations (Lesotho)
a7227.speech: Told the Lesotho Times that former ambassadors had been invited to participate in the workshop "to share their expertise, experiences, and ideas with the current envoys" ; "They have been on this journey and know better, so they can provide guidance on how to successfully execute their roles."

a7227.speaker: Kutloano Pheko, Principal Information Officer of the Ministry of Foreign Affairs and International Relations (Lesotho)
a7227.speech: When quizzed on the rumours of reshuffling of the ambassadors after the workshop, said that had not been the primary reason for the consultations; however, he acknowledged that "reshuffling can happen at any time".

a7227.speaker: King Letsie III of Lesotho (Speech from the Throne, November 2022)
a7227.speech: Placed emphasis on the importance of Lesotho "deploying diplomatic professionals who can secure lucrative benefits for the country when they are deployed to foreign missions."

a7227.speaker: Lejone Mpotjoane, Minister of Foreign Affairs and International Relations (Lesotho)
a7227.speech: Emphasized the importance of this initiative during his opening remarks: "Under the new leadership (of Prime Minister Sam Matekane's coalition administration), we have not had sufficient time to consult on the new vision that the government has for Lesotho" ; said the workshop was meant to "equip diplomatic representatives with the knowledge and strategies necessary to promote international trade, enhance tourism, and improve productivity in the energy sector, among other priorities."

a7227.speaker: Lejone Mpotjoane, Minister of Foreign Affairs and International Relations (Lesotho)
a7227.speech: Noted the urgency of addressing the country's high unemployment rates and the interconnected issues of crime and corruption that stemmed from low productivity levels: "One of our key goals is to increase productivity, particularly in agriculture, with the support of our diplomatic missions and international partners" ; further underscored the need for skills exportation as one of the ways to address the high unemployment in Lesotho.

a7227.speaker: Lejone Mpotjoane, Minister of Foreign Affairs and International Relations (Lesotho)
a7227.speech: Highlighting Lesotho's abundant natural resources, said the country's potential to produce and export electricity to meet the growing demands in the Southern African region was one of its low hanging fruits to be plucked to improve prosperity levels for citizens.

a7227.speaker: Lejone Mpotjoane, Minister of Foreign Affairs and International Relations (Lesotho)
a7227.speech: Reiterated a significant policy shift aimed at boosting tourism by offering visa-free entry to European Union citizens: "This decision is expected to foster unparalleled growth in tourism and international relations."

a7227.speaker: Lejone Mpotjoane, Minister of Foreign Affairs and International Relations (Lesotho)
a7227.speech: Expressed the need to revise Lesotho's foreign policy "in light of evolving geopolitical realities": "We must work together with you, our diplomatic missions, to navigate this changing landscape," he urged, revealing plans to establish the Lesotho Institute of Diplomacy, which he said aims to fortify the diplomatic profession and better address the challenges it faces.

a7227.speaker: Lejone Mpotjoane, Minister of Foreign Affairs and International Relations (Lesotho)
a7227.speech: Addressed the impact of external factors on Lesotho's economy, particularly recent developments regarding U.S. aid, and stressed the necessity for a strategic government vision to build Lesotho's economic resilience: "The current environment necessitates a transformative approach to promote trade, investment, and tourism, which hold the keys to our economic diplomacy."

a7366.speaker: Yusuf Tuggar, Nigeria's Minister of Foreign Affairs
a7366.speech: Stated that allegations of the United States Agency for International Development (USAID) supporting Boko Haram remain unproven, and emphasised that the Nigerian government also did not want to meddle in US politics, alluding that the allegation first came from a politician: "With regards to the dignity of Nigeria and this allegation - it is an allegation, it's not something that has been proven. And we know that politics is also played in the United States of America. They have partisan politics. It's not our business. We're not getting involved in their domestic politics."

a7366.speaker: Yusuf Tuggar, Nigeria's Minister of Foreign Affairs
a7366.speech: Reassured Nigerians that despite the allegations, the terrorist group has been significantly weakened, and highlighted ongoing efforts to rehabilitate and reintegrate affected individuals through government initiatives; he pointed to the government's Safe Corridor programme in Gombe, where former militants, combatants, and non-combatants are assessed and provided with the necessary support, and said individuals are categorised based on their level of involvement, with some being reoriented, others facing trial, and those in need of resettlement receiving assistance.

a7366.speaker: Yusuf Tuggar, Nigeria's Minister of Foreign Affairs
a7366.speech: Praised Nigeria's counterterrorism strategies, particularly the Multinational Joint Task Force (MNJTF), which he said has become a model for other nations: "Somalia is looking at what we're doing, saying they want to copy us, and several others. Sometimes, we take for granted some of the homegrown solutions we come up with. The Multinational Joint Task Force is being studied by developed countries, asking, 'How are these guys doing it?' We want to do the same thing."

a7366.speaker: Yusuf Tuggar, Nigeria's Minister of Foreign Affairs
a7366.speech: Highlighted Nigeria's longstanding contributions to peacekeeping missions across Africa, citing past efforts in Sierra Leone and Liberia, and urged Nigerians to recognise the country's achievements in security and diplomacy: "We really need to start looking at ourselves differently. We need to start looking at our model and our applications. We need to start looking at what we did with regards to peacebuilding in Sierra Leone, in Liberia, and what we're doing now in the Northeast."

a7460.speaker: Communique of the Council of Ministers of Wednesday 5 February
a7460.speech: Made public the two ordinances, not yet signed, as bills and, as such, therefore having to be submitted to the CNT, the legislative organ of the Transition.

a7460.speaker: Prime Minister of Mali
a7460.speech: At a press briefing at the Prime Minister's Office, asserted with a noticeable touch of irritation that the famous ordinances were not effective for the time being - and was contradicted by the publication of the two documents, both bearing the date of 7 February 2025.

a7460.speaker: Alousseni Sanou, Minister of the Economy and Finance, and the Prime Minister (press briefing)
a7460.speech: The two speakers merely confirmed what Malians had understood and decried, namely the levies presented as national contribution and solidarity.

a7460.speaker: Sekou Tounkara, US-based activist
a7460.speech: Recent "revelations" which, if verified, are an indication that management at the top already suffers from a lack of transparency and of trust between the high-perched actors.

a7460.speaker: Jurists (unnamed)
a7460.speech: Add that we are in a legal imbroglio between two conflicting provisions in the new constitution on the imprescriptibility of the military coup d'Etat in its relation to the benefit of an amnesty, combined with the future consequences of the possibility of nullity of the administrative and legislative acts taken by the actors of the transition, risking an unprecedented crisis if correction by constitutional amendment is not envisaged.

a7460.speaker: Enabling law 2024-038 (CNT)
a7460.speech: The CNT authorised the government to take certain ordinances; but among these ordinances the creation of taxes and contributions does not figure.
